articles.title: Filled Julia set
articles.statement:
For $c \in \mathbb{C}$, let $T_c(z) = z^2 + c$ and let $T_c^n$ be its
$n$-fold iterate. The filled Julia set $K_c$ is the set of $z \in \mathbb{C}$ whose orbit under
$T_c$ is bounded: there is a real $M$ such that $|T_c^n(z)| \le M$ for every $n \ge 0$.

articles.title: Fatou–Julia dichotomy for quadratic polynomials
articles.statement:
For $c \in \mathbb{C}$, let $K_c$ be the
filled Julia set of $T_c(z) = z^2 + c$ and let $M$ be the Mandelbrot set. If $c \in M$, then $K_c$
is nonempty and connected. If $c \notin M$, then $K_c$ is homeomorphic to the Cantor space
$\{0, 1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$ of binary sequences with the product topology.

## Sources

- P. Fatou, *Sur les équations fonctionnelles*, Bull. Soc. Math. France 47 (1919), 161-271; 48 (1920), 33-94, 208-314. G. Julia, *Mémoire sur l'itération des fonctions rationnelles*, J. Math. Pures Appl. 1 (1918), 47-245. Modern statement: A. Douady and J. H. Hubbard, *Étude dynamique des polynômes complexes I, II*, Publ. Math. Orsay 84-02, 85-04. Listed as §62 (additional statement 1) in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `fatou_julia_dichotomy` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Mandelbrot set of the quadratic family
articles.statement:
Let $T_c(z) = z^2 + c$ for $c \in \mathbb{C}$
and let $T_c^n$ be its $n$-fold iterate. The Mandelbrot set $M$ is the set of $c \in \mathbb{C}$
for which the orbit of $0$ under $T_c$ is bounded: there is a real $R$ such that
$|T_c^n(0)| \le R$ for every $n \ge 0$.

articles.title: Quadratic map $T_c$
articles.statement:
For $c \in \mathbb{C}$, $T_c \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is the
map $T_c(z) = z^2 + c$.

articles.title: Mandelbrot set
articles.statement:
The Mandelbrot set is the set $M$ of complex numbers $c$ for which the orbit
of $0$ under the quadratic map $T_c(z) = z^2 + c$ is bounded: there is a real number $R$ with
$|T_c^n(0)| \le R$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, where $T_c^n$ is the $n$-th iterate of $T_c$ and
$T_c^0$ is the identity.

articles.title: Hausdorff dimension of the Mandelbrot boundary (Shishikura)
articles.statement:
The boundary of the
Mandelbrot set $M \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ has Hausdorff dimension $2$.

## Sources

- M. Shishikura, The Hausdorff dimension of the boundary of the Mandelbrot set and Julia sets, Ann. of Math. 147 (1998). Listed as §260 in O. Knill, Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Knill, §260. Problem `mandelbrot_boundary_dimh` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The Mandelbrot set is connected (Douady–Hubbard)
articles.statement:
The Mandelbrot set, the set of all
$c \in \mathbb{C}$ for which the sequence $(T_c^n(0))_{n \ge 0}$ of iterates of $0$ under
$T_c(z) = z^2 + c$ is bounded, is a nonempty connected subset of $\mathbb{C}$.

## Sources

- A. Douady and J. H. Hubbard, *Étude dynamique des polynômes complexes I, II*, Publ. Math. Orsay 84-02, 85-04. Listed as §62 in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `mandelbrot_connected` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The Mandelbrot set
articles.statement:
The Mandelbrot set is the set of all $c \in \mathbb{C}$ for which the
orbit of $0$ under $T_c(z) = z^2 + c$ is bounded: there is a real number $M$ with
$|T_c^n(0)| \le M$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, where $T_c^n$ is the $n$-th iterate of $T_c$
and $T_c^0$ is the identity.

articles.title: Quadratic family
articles.statement:
For each complex number $c$, the map $T_c : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is
given by $T_c(z) = z^2 + c$.

articles.title: The quadratic family
articles.statement:
For $c \in \mathbb{C}$, $T_c \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is the
map $T_c(z) = z^2 + c$.

articles.title: Basin of attraction of zero
articles.statement:
For $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$, the basin of zero of
$f_\lambda(z) = \lambda z^2 + z^3$ is the set of $z \in \mathbb{C}$ whose forward orbit tends to
$0$, that is, $f_\lambda^{n}(z) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$, where $f_\lambda^{n}$ denotes the
$n$-th iterate of $f_\lambda$.

## Sources

- [AMR-052-0019], Stony Brook open problems (1992), McMullen III.2.

articles.title: Roesch's theorem on the boundaries of cubic parameter components
articles.statement:
For the cubic family
$f_\lambda(z) = \lambda z^2 + z^3$ with $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$, the boundary of every parameter
component is a Jordan curve. Here a parameter component is a connected component of the set of
$\lambda$ for which every critical point of $f_\lambda$ lies in the immediate basin of zero of
$f_\lambda$.

Roesch (Theorem 2) proves that the boundary of every component of
$H = \{a : -a \text{ lies in the basin of } 0\}$ for the family $z^{d-1}(z + da/(d-1))$ is a
Jordan curve; at $d = 3$ the linear change $\lambda = 3a/2$ carries the central component $H_0$
onto the parameter component.

## Sources

- Pascale Roesch, Hyperbolic components of polynomials with a fixed critical point of maximal order, Ann. Sci. Ecole Norm. Sup. (4) 40 (2007), arXiv:math/0612172, https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0612172.

articles.title: McMullen's question on Jordan boundaries of cubic parameter components
articles.statement:
Let
$f_\lambda(z) = \lambda z^2 + z^3$ for $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$. The statement is that for every
parameter component $U$, that is, every connected component of the set of $\lambda$ for which
every critical point of $f_\lambda$ lies in the immediate basin of zero of $f_\lambda$, the
boundary $\partial U$ of $U$ in $\mathbb{C}$ is a Jordan curve.

The source poses this as an open question.

## Sources

- [AMR-052-0019], Stony Brook open problems (1992), McMullen III.2.

articles.title: Cubic family
articles.statement:
For a parameter $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$, the cubic polynomial map
$f_\lambda : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is given by $f_\lambda(z) = \lambda z^2 + z^3$.

## Sources

- [AMR-052-0019], Stony Brook open problems (1992), McMullen III.2.

articles.title: Critical points of the cubic family
articles.statement:
For $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$, a point
$c \in \mathbb{C}$ is a critical point of $f_\lambda(z) = \lambda z^2 + z^3$ when $f_\lambda$ has
complex derivative $0$ at $c$, that is, $f_\lambda'(c) = 0$.

## Sources

- [AMR-052-0019], Stony Brook open problems (1992), McMullen III.2.

articles.title: Immediate basin of zero
articles.statement:
For $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$, a set $V \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ is
the immediate basin of zero of $f_\lambda(z) = \lambda z^2 + z^3$ when $0 \in V$, $V$ is contained
in the basin of zero of $f_\lambda$ (the set of $z$ with $f_\lambda^{n}(z) \to 0$), $V$ is
connected, and every connected set $W \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ with $0 \in W$ that is contained in the
basin of zero of $f_\lambda$ satisfies $W \subseteq V$. Thus $V$ is the connected component of $0$
in the basin of zero.

## Sources

- [AMR-052-0019], Stony Brook open problems (1992), McMullen III.2.

articles.title: Jordan curves in the plane
articles.statement:
A set $S \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ is a Jordan curve when there is
a continuous injective map $f$ from the unit circle $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| = 1\}$ to
$\mathbb{C}$ whose image is exactly $S$.

## Sources

- [AMR-052-0019], Stony Brook open problems (1992), McMullen III.2.

articles.title: Parameter components
articles.statement:
A set $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ is a parameter component when it is
a connected component of the parameter set, the set of $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ for which every
critical point of $f_\lambda(z) = \lambda z^2 + z^3$ lies in the immediate basin of zero of
$f_\lambda$: $U$ is nonempty, contained in the parameter set and connected, and every connected
set $W \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ with $U \subseteq W$ that is contained in the parameter set equals
$U$.

## Sources

- [AMR-052-0019], Stony Brook open problems (1992), McMullen III.2.

articles.title: Parameters with both critical points in the immediate basin
articles.statement:
The parameter set is the set
of $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ for which some immediate basin of zero $V$ of
$f_\lambda(z) = \lambda z^2 + z^3$ contains every critical point of $f_\lambda$.

Since $f_\lambda'(z) = z(3z + 2\lambda)$, the critical points of $f_\lambda$ are $0$ and
$-2\lambda/3$ (equal when $\lambda = 0$), so this asks that both finite critical points lie in
the immediate basin of zero.

## Sources

- [AMR-052-0019], Stony Brook open problems (1992), McMullen III.2.

articles.title: Diophantine real numbers
articles.statement:
A real number $\alpha$ is Diophantine if there are real numbers
$C > 0$ and $\tau$ such that $C / |q|^{\tau} \le |\alpha - p/q|$ for all integers $p$ and $q$
with $q \neq 0$.

Any such exponent $\tau$ is at least $2$, by Dirichlet's approximation theorem. A Diophantine
$\alpha$ is irrational, so $e^{2\pi i \alpha}$ is not a root of unity.

articles.title: Poincaré–Siegel linearisation theorem
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a Diophantine real number and let
$\lambda = e^{2\pi i \alpha}$. If $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is analytic at $0$ with
$f(0) = 0$ and $f'(0) = \lambda$, then there is a function $u : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$,
analytic at $0$ with $u(0) = 0$ and $u'(0) = 1$, such that $f(u(z)) = u(\lambda z)$ for all $z$
in some neighbourhood of $0$.

## Sources

- C. L. Siegel, *Iteration of analytic functions*, Annals of Math. 43 (1942), 607-612. Earlier formal-power-series version: H. Poincaré thèse (1879). Listed as §83 (additional statement 1) in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `poincare_siegel_linearisation` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The Mandelbar set is not path-connected
articles.statement:
The Mandelbar set (tricorn), the set of
$c \in \mathbb{C}$ for which the orbit of $0$ under $z \mapsto \bar z^2 + c$ is bounded, is not
path-connected.

This is the degree-2 case of the Hubbard–Schleicher theorem that multicorns are not
path-connected.

## Sources

- John H. Hubbard and Dierk Schleicher, *Multicorns are not Path Connected*, arXiv:1209.1753 (2012); published in *Frontiers in Complex Dynamics* (Princeton University Press, 2014), pp. 73-102. Listed as §62 (additional statement 2) in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `mandelbar_not_path_connected` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The Mandelbar set (tricorn)
articles.statement:
The Mandelbar set is the set of $c \in \mathbb{C}$ for which
the orbit of $0$ under the map $T_c(z) = \bar z^2 + c$ is bounded: there is a real number $M$
with $|T_c^n(0)| \le M$ for all $n \ge 0$, where $T_c^n$ is the $n$-th iterate of $T_c$ and
$T_c^0$ is the identity.

This set is the connectedness locus of the family $z \mapsto \bar z^2 + c$.

articles.title: The antiholomorphic quadratic map
articles.statement:
For $c \in \mathbb{C}$, the map
$T_c : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is $T_c(z) = \bar z^2 + c$, where $\bar z$ is the complex
conjugate of $z$.

articles.title: Bilinear polynomial ergodic averages
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a measurable space and let
$T : X \to X$ be a measurable bijection with measurable inverse. For a real number $N \ge 0$,
polynomials $P_1, P_2 \in \mathbb{Z}[t]$, functions $f, g : X \to \mathbb{C}$ and a point
$x \in X$, the bilinear average is the complex number

$$A_N^{P_1, P_2}(f, g)(x) = \frac{1}{\lfloor N \rfloor}
\sum_{n=1}^{\lfloor N \rfloor} f(T^{P_1(n)} x)\, g(T^{P_2(n)} x),$$

where $T^k$ for $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ is the $k$-th power of $T$ in the group of bijections of $X$
(so negative powers are iterates of $T^{-1}$), and $A_N^{P_1, P_2}(f, g)(x) = 0$ when
$\lfloor N \rfloor = 0$.

articles.title: Lacunary sequence
articles.statement:
For a real number $\Lambda \ge 0$, a sequence
$(a_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonnegative real numbers is $\Lambda$-lacunary if
$a_{n+1} / a_n > \Lambda$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, where division by $0$ gives $0$; in
particular every term of a $\Lambda$-lacunary sequence is positive.

articles.title: Mean ergodic theorem for bilinear polynomial averages
articles.statement:
Let $(X, \mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite
measure space and let $T : X \to X$ be a measurable bijection with measurable inverse that
preserves $\mu$. Let $P \in \mathbb{Z}[t]$ have degree at least $2$, and let
$p_1, p_2 \in (1, \infty)$ and $p \in [0, \infty]$ satisfy $p_1^{-1} + p_2^{-1} = p^{-1}$ and
$p^{-1} \le 1$. For a real number $N \ge 0$, functions $f, g : X \to \mathbb{C}$ and $x \in X$ let

$$A_N(f, g)(x) = \frac{1}{\lfloor N \rfloor}
\sum_{n=1}^{\lfloor N \rfloor} f(T^n x)\, g(T^{P(n)} x),$$

with $A_N(f, g)(x) = 0$ when $\lfloor N \rfloor = 0$, where $T^k$ for $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ is the
$k$-th power of $T$ in the group of bijections of $X$. Then for all
$f \in L^{p_1}(\mu)$ and $g \in L^{p_2}(\mu)$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$ there is a function
$h : X \to \mathbb{C}$ in $L^p(\mu)$ such that $\|A_N(f, g) - h\|_{L^p(\mu)} \to 0$ as the real
number $N$ tends to $\infty$.

This is Theorem 1.17(i) of Krause, Mirek and Tao.

## Sources

- B. Krause, M. Mirek, and T. Tao, `Pointwise ergodic theorems for non-conventional bilinear polynomial averages`, Annals of Math, 195 (3) 2022. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_pointwise_ergodic_theorems` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Pointwise ergodic theorem for bilinear polynomial averages
articles.statement:
Let $(X, \mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite
measure space and let $T : X \to X$ be a measurable bijection with measurable inverse that
preserves $\mu$. Let $P \in \mathbb{Z}[t]$ have degree at least $2$, and let
$p_1, p_2 \in (1, \infty)$ and $p \in [0, \infty]$ satisfy $p_1^{-1} + p_2^{-1} = p^{-1}$ and
$p^{-1} \le 1$. For a real number $N \ge 0$, functions $f, g : X \to \mathbb{C}$ and $x \in X$ let

$$A_N(f, g)(x) = \frac{1}{\lfloor N \rfloor}
\sum_{n=1}^{\lfloor N \rfloor} f(T^n x)\, g(T^{P(n)} x),$$

with $A_N(f, g)(x) = 0$ when $\lfloor N \rfloor = 0$, where $T^k$ for $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ is the
$k$-th power of $T$ in the group of bijections of $X$. Then for
all $f \in L^{p_1}(\mu)$ and $g \in L^{p_2}(\mu)$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$ there is a function
$h : X \to \mathbb{C}$ in $L^p(\mu)$ such that for $\mu$-almost every $x \in X$,
$A_N(f, g)(x) \to h(x)$ as the real number $N$ tends to $\infty$.

This is Theorem 1.17(ii) of Krause, Mirek and Tao.

## Sources

- B. Krause, M. Mirek, and T. Tao, `Pointwise ergodic theorems for non-conventional bilinear polynomial averages`, Annals of Math, 195 (3) 2022. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_pointwise_ergodic_theorems` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Maximal inequality for bilinear polynomial averages
articles.statement:
Let $(X, \mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite
measure space and let $T : X \to X$ be a measurable bijection with measurable inverse that
preserves $\mu$. Let $P \in \mathbb{Z}[t]$ have degree at least $2$, and let
$p_1, p_2 \in (1, \infty)$ and $p \in [0, \infty]$ satisfy $p_1^{-1} + p_2^{-1} = p^{-1}$ and
$p^{-1} \le 1$. For a real number $N \ge 0$, functions $f, g : X \to \mathbb{C}$ and $x \in X$ let

$$A_N(f, g)(x) = \frac{1}{\lfloor N \rfloor}
\sum_{n=1}^{\lfloor N \rfloor} f(T^n x)\, g(T^{P(n)} x),$$

with $A_N(f, g)(x) = 0$ when $\lfloor N \rfloor = 0$, where $T^k$ for $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ is the
$k$-th power of $T$ in the group of bijections of $X$. Then there is
a constant $C \ge 0$, which may depend on $(X, \mu, T)$, $P$, $p_1$, $p_2$ and $p$, such that
for all $f \in L^{p_1}(\mu)$ and $g \in L^{p_2}(\mu)$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$,

$$\Big\| \sup_{N \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}} |A_N(f, g)| \Big\|_{L^p(\mu)} \le
C \, \|f\|_{L^{p_1}(\mu)} \, \|g\|_{L^{p_2}(\mu)},$$

where the supremum is taken pointwise in $[0, \infty]$.

This is Theorem 1.17(iii) of Krause, Mirek and Tao.

## Sources

- B. Krause, M. Mirek, and T. Tao, `Pointwise ergodic theorems for non-conventional bilinear polynomial averages`, Annals of Math, 195 (3) 2022. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_pointwise_ergodic_theorems` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Long variational inequality for bilinear polynomial averages
articles.statement:
Let $(X, \mu)$ be a
$\sigma$-finite measure space and let $T : X \to X$ be a measurable bijection with measurable
inverse that preserves $\mu$. Let $P \in \mathbb{Z}[t]$ have degree at least $2$, and let
$p_1, p_2 \in (1, \infty)$ and $p \in [0, \infty]$ satisfy $p_1^{-1} + p_2^{-1} = p^{-1}$ and
$p^{-1} \le 1$. For a real number $N \ge 0$, functions $f, g : X \to \mathbb{C}$ and $x \in X$ let

$$A_N(f, g)(x) = \frac{1}{\lfloor N \rfloor}
\sum_{n=1}^{\lfloor N \rfloor} f(T^n x)\, g(T^{P(n)} x),$$

with $A_N(f, g)(x) = 0$ when $\lfloor N \rfloor = 0$, where $T^k$ for $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ is the
$k$-th power of $T$ in the group of bijections of $X$. Then
for all real numbers $r > 2$ and $\Lambda > 1$ there is a constant $C \ge 0$, which may depend
on $r$, $\Lambda$ and all of the data above, such that for all $f \in L^{p_1}(\mu)$ and
$g \in L^{p_2}(\mu)$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$ and every $\Lambda$-lacunary sequence
$(a_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonnegative reals (that is, $a_{n+1} / a_n > \Lambda$ for all $n$)
with $a_n \ge 1$ for all $n$,

$$\Big\| x \mapsto \big\| (A_{a_n}(f, g)(x))_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \big\|_{\mathbb{V}^r}
\Big\|_{L^p(\mu)} \le C \, \|f\|_{L^{p_1}(\mu)} \, \|g\|_{L^{p_2}(\mu)},$$

where $\| \cdot \|_{\mathbb{V}^r}$ is the $r$-variational norm of a sequence of complex numbers.

This is Theorem 1.17(iv) of Krause, Mirek and Tao.

## Sources

- B. Krause, M. Mirek, and T. Tao, `Pointwise ergodic theorems for non-conventional bilinear polynomial averages`, Annals of Math, 195 (3) 2022. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_pointwise_ergodic_theorems` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Variational norm
articles.statement:
For a real number $r \ge 0$ and a sequence
$a = (a_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of complex numbers, the $r$-variational norm of $a$ is the
element of $[0, \infty]$

$$\|a\|_{\mathbb{V}^r} = \sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} |a_n| +
\sup_{J \in \mathbb{N}} \sup_{N_0 \le N_1 \le \dots \le N_J}
\Big( \sum_{j=0}^{J-1} |a_{N_{j+1}} - a_{N_j}|^r \Big)^{1/r},$$

where the inner supremum runs over nondecreasing finite sequences of natural numbers
$N_0 \le N_1 \le \dots \le N_J$ and the empty sum ($J = 0$) is $0$. For $r = 0$ the whole term
$\big( \sum_{j=0}^{J-1} |a_{N_{j+1}} - a_{N_j}|^r \big)^{1/r}$ is replaced by the number of
indices $j < J$ with $a_{N_{j+1}} \ne a_{N_j}$.

articles.title: Monotonicity of Birkhoff averages
articles.statement:
Let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ be a map. For
$u : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, $n \ge 1$ and $x \in \alpha$, write
$A_n u(x) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} u(T^k x)$ for the $n$-th Birkhoff average of $u$ at
$x$, and $A_0 u(x) = 0$. If $u, v : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $u(y) \le v(y)$ for every
$y \in \alpha$, then $A_n u(x) \le A_n v(x)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every
$x \in \alpha$.

articles.title: Birkhoff's ergodic theorem in $L^1$ (ergodic case)
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure
on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ be ergodic with respect to $\mu$ (in
particular $T$ preserves $\mu$), and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$-integrable. For
$n \ge 1$ let $A_n g(x) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$ be the Birkhoff averages of
$g$. Then $\int \left| A_n g(x) - \int g \, d\mu \right| d\mu(x) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$; that
is, the Birkhoff averages of $g$ converge to the constant $\int g \, d\mu$ in $L^1(\mu)$.

articles.title: Birkhoff limit is a conditional expectation on invariant sets
articles.statement: The Birkhoff limit is the conditional expectation of `f` given the invariant σ-algebra.

articles.title: Birkhoff limit of an ergodic map is the space average
articles.statement:
For ergodic `T` on a probability space the Birkhoff limit is the constant `∫ f dμ`; this is
`MathlibExt.Dynamics.Ergodic.BirkhoffWanted.birkhoff_pointwise_ergodic` combined with
`tendsto_birkhoffAverage_ae`.

articles.title: Birkhoff limit of a function
articles.statement:
The limit of the Birkhoff averages of `f` (defined as `f*` cast to `ℝ`; it is the limit
almost everywhere by `tendsto_birkhoffAverage_ae`).

articles.title: Birkhoff pointwise ergodic theorem (ergodic case)
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a
measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ be ergodic with respect to $\mu$ (in
particular $T$ preserves $\mu$), and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$-integrable. Then for
$\mu$-almost every $x \in \alpha$, the Birkhoff averages $\frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$
converge to $\int g \, d\mu$ as $n \to \infty$.

## Sources

- G. D. Birkhoff, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 17 (1931); Walters, Intro to Ergodic Theory; Lean states ergodic case for ℝ-valued integrable functions while general theorem gives conditional expectation onto invariant σ-algebra.

articles.title: Invariance of the maximal divergence set
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a measurable space. For every map
$T : \alpha \to \alpha$, every function $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ and every real number $c$, the
preimage under $T$ of the maximal divergence set of $T$, $g$ and $c$ equals that set.

articles.title: Invariance of the maximal divergence set under iterates
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a measurable
space, $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ a map, $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ a function and $c$ a real number.
For every natural number $k$ and every $x \in \alpha$, the point $T^k x$ lies in the maximal
divergence set of $T$, $g$ and $c$ if and only if $x$ does.

articles.title: Measurability of the maximal divergence set
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space
$\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be
measurable. Then for every real number $c$, the maximal divergence set of $T$, $g$ and $c$ is a
measurable set.

articles.title: Membership in the maximal divergence set
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a measurable space,
$T : \alpha \to \alpha$ a map, $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ a function, $c$ a real number and
$x \in \alpha$. Then $x$ lies in the maximal divergence set of $T$, $g$ and $c$ if and only if
there is a rational number $q > c$ such that for every natural number $N$ there is a natural
number $n \ge N$ with $n q < \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$.

articles.title: Maximal divergence set
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a measurable space, $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ a map,
$g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ a function and $c$ a real number. The maximal divergence set of $T$,
$g$ and $c$ is the set of points $x \in \alpha$ for which there is a rational number $q > c$ such
that $n q < \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$ for infinitely many natural numbers $n$.

articles.title: Birkhoff sums of a function cut off to an invariant set, inside the set
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a
measurable space, $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ a map, $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ a function, $c$ a real
number, and $D \subseteq \alpha$ a set such that for every natural number $k$ and every
$x \in \alpha$, $T^k x \in D$ if and only if $x \in D$. Let $h : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy
$h(y) = g(y) - c$ for $y \in D$ and $h(y) = 0$ for $y \notin D$. Then for every $x \in D$ and
every natural number $n$, $\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} h(T^k x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x) - n c$.

articles.title: Birkhoff sums of a function cut off to an invariant set, outside the set
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be
a measurable space, $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ a map, $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ a function, $c$ a
real number, and $D \subseteq \alpha$ a set such that for every natural number $k$ and every
$x \in \alpha$, $T^k x \in D$ if and only if $x \in D$. Let $h : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy
$h(y) = g(y) - c$ for $y \in D$ and $h(y) = 0$ for $y \notin D$. Then for every $x \notin D$ and
every natural number $n$, $\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} h(T^k x) = 0$.

articles.title: Birkhoff averages are L1 contractions
articles.statement:
Birkhoff averages are `L¹`-contractions. See also
`MathlibExt.Probability.BirkhoffErgodicL1.integral_norm_birkhoffAverage_sub_le`, the same bound
for differences, stated with integrals of norms.

articles.title: Upper limit of Birkhoff averages is invariant
articles.statement: The upper limit of the Birkhoff averages is `T`-invariant.

articles.title: Lower limit of Birkhoff averages
articles.statement: The lower limit `liminf_n A_n f x` of the Birkhoff averages, in `EReal`.

articles.title: Upper limit of Birkhoff averages
articles.statement: The upper limit `limsup_n A_n f x` of the Birkhoff averages, in `EReal`.

articles.title: Maximal ergodic theorem
articles.statement:
**Maximal ergodic theorem** (E. Hopf, 1954), in the finite form of A. M. Garsia, *A simple
proof of E. Hopf's maximal ergodic theorem*, 1965: for measure-preserving `T` and integrable `f`,
the integral of `f` over `{max_{1 ≤ n ≤ N} S_n f > 0}` is nonnegative. See also
`MathlibExt.Dynamics.Ergodic.BirkhoffWanted.maximal_ergodic`, the limiting form for measurable
`f`.

articles.title: Integrability of Birkhoff averages
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space
$\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be
$\mu$-integrable. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ the Birkhoff average
$x \mapsto \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$ is $\mu$-integrable (for $n = 0$ it is the
zero function).

articles.title: Integrability of the Birkhoff limit
articles.statement: The Birkhoff limit of an integrable function is integrable.

articles.title: Integrability of Birkhoff sums
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$,
let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be
$\mu$-integrable. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ the Birkhoff sum
$x \mapsto \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$ is $\mu$-integrable.

articles.title: Birkhoff averages preserve the integral
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space
$\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $u : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be
$\mu$-integrable. Then for every $n \ge 1$,
$\int \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} u(T^k x) \, d\mu(x) = \int u \, d\mu$.

articles.title: Invariance of the integral under iterates
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space
$\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $u : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be
$\mu$-integrable. Then for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, writing $T^k$ for the $k$-th iterate of
$T$, we have $\int u(T^k x) \, d\mu(x) = \int u \, d\mu$.

articles.title: Birkhoff averages are $L^1$-contractions
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space
$\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $g, h : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be
$\mu$-integrable. For a function $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ and $n \ge 1$ write
$A_n f(x) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(T^k x)$, and $A_0 f = 0$. Then for every
$n \in \mathbb{N}$,
$\int |A_n g(x) - A_n h(x)| \, d\mu(x) \le \int |g(x) - h(x)| \, d\mu(x)$.

articles.title: Invariant set as a set equal to its preimage
articles.statement:
`IsInvariantSet T E` is the condition `T ⁻¹' E = E` used by Mathlib's `PreErgodic` and
`MeasurableSpace.invariants`.

articles.title: Invariant set of a map
articles.statement:
`E` is invariant under `T`: `x ∈ E ↔ T x ∈ E`, i.e. `T ⁻¹' E = E`
(see `isInvariantSet_iff_preimage_eq`).

articles.title: Invariant set is invariant under every iterate
articles.statement: An invariant set is invariant under every iterate.

articles.title: Oscillation set of Birkhoff averages
articles.statement:
The invariant set `{f_* < a} ∩ {b < f*}` where the Birkhoff averages oscillate across
`[a, b]`.

articles.title: Maximal Birkhoff partial sum
articles.statement: The maximal Birkhoff sum `max_{1 ≤ n ≤ N} ∑_{k<n} f (T^[k] x)` over the first `N` times.

articles.title: Hopf maximal ergodic theorem
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on a measurable space $\alpha$,
let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be measurable and
$\mu$-integrable. For a natural number $n$ write $S_n f(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(T^k x)$. Then the
integral of $f$ with respect to $\mu$ over the set of points $x \in \alpha$ such that
$S_n f(x) > 0$ for some natural number $n$ is nonnegative.

articles.title: Oscillation set of Birkhoff averages is null
articles.statement: For `a < b` the oscillation set `levelSet T f a b` is null.

articles.title: Triangle inequality for Birkhoff averages
articles.statement:
Let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ be a map. For
$f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ and $n \ge 1$ write $A_n f(x) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(T^k x)$
for the $n$-th Birkhoff average of $f$, and $A_0 f = 0$. Then for every
$u : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $x \in \alpha$, writing $|u|$ for
the function $y \mapsto |u(y)|$, we have $|A_n u(x)| \le A_n |u|(x)$.

articles.title: Birkhoff averages of a bounded function are bounded
articles.statement:
Let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ be a
map, let $M \ge 0$, and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $|g(x)| \le M$ for every
$x \in \alpha$. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $x \in \alpha$, the Birkhoff average
$\frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$ (taken to be $0$ for $n = 0$) has absolute value at
most $M$.

articles.title: Birkhoff limit preserves integrals over invariant sets
articles.statement: On every measurable invariant set `E`, `∫_E birkhoffLimit T f dμ = ∫_E f dμ`.

articles.title: Maximal ergodic inequality on an invariant set
articles.statement:
The maximal inequality on an invariant set: if every point of the invariant set `E` has
some positive Birkhoff sum of `g`, then `∫_E g dμ ≥ 0`.

articles.title: Birkhoff averages converge almost everywhere to the Birkhoff limit
articles.statement: The Birkhoff averages of an integrable `f` converge a.e. to `birkhoffLimit T f`.

articles.title: Birkhoff's pointwise ergodic theorem
articles.statement:
**Birkhoff's pointwise ergodic theorem** (G. D. Birkhoff, *Proof of the ergodic theorem*,
1931): for `T` preserving a finite measure `μ` and integrable `f`, the averages
`(1/n) ∑_{k<n} f ∘ T^k` converge `μ`-a.e. to `μ[f | MeasurableSpace.invariants T]`. See also
`MathlibExt.Dynamics.Ergodic.BirkhoffWanted.birkhoff_pointwise_ergodic`, the ergodic case, and
`birkhoffLimit_ae_eq_integral_of_ergodic`.

articles.title: Birkhoff's ergodic theorem in $L^1$ for bounded functions
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability
measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ be ergodic with respect to
$\mu$ (in particular $T$ preserves $\mu$), let $M \ge 0$, and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be
$\mu$-integrable with $|g(x)| \le M$ for every $x \in \alpha$. For $n \ge 1$ let
$A_n g(x) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$. Then
$\int \left| A_n g(x) - \int g \, d\mu \right| d\mu(x) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.

This follows from the almost-everywhere ergodic theorem and dominated convergence.

articles.title: Bourgain's polynomial ergodic theorem
articles.statement:
Let $(X, \mu)$ be a probability space, let
$T : X \to X$ be a measure-preserving map, let $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be an integer
polynomial sequence, and let $f : X \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function in $L^p(\mu)$ for some
$p$ with $1 < p < \infty$. Then there is a function $F : X \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for
$\mu$-almost every $x \in X$ the polynomial ergodic averages
$\frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(T^{a(k)}(x))$, $n \ge 1$, where $T^{a(k)}$ is the $a(k)$-fold
iterate of $T$, converge to $F(x)$ as $n \to \infty$.

## Sources

- J. Bourgain, *Pointwise ergodic theorems for arithmetic sets*, Publ. Math. IHÉS 69 (1989). Knill, *Some fundamental theorems in mathematics*, §173. Problem `bourgain_polynomial_ergodic` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Integer polynomial sequences
articles.statement:
A sequence $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is an integer
polynomial sequence if there is a polynomial $P$ with integer coefficients such that
$P(n) \ge 0$ and $a(n) = P(n)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

articles.title: Polynomial ergodic averages
articles.statement:
Given a sequence $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, a map
$T : X \to X$, a function $f : X \to \mathbb{R}$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $x \in X$, the $n$-th
polynomial ergodic average of $f$ at $x$ is

$$\frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f\bigl(T^{a(k)}(x)\bigr),$$

where $T^{a(k)}$ is the $a(k)$-fold iterate of $T$; for $n = 0$ the average is $0$.

articles.title: Furstenberg multiple recurrence theorem
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable
space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ be a measurable map preserving $\mu$, and let $A$ be a
measurable set with $\mu(A) > 0$. For $m \in \mathbb{N}$ write $T^{-m}(A)$ for the preimage of $A$
under the $m$-th iterate of $T$. Then for every integer $k > 0$ there is an integer $n > 0$ such
that

$$\mu\Big(\bigcap_{i=0}^{k-1} T^{-i n}(A)\Big) > 0.$$

Proof: We apply the finitary Szemerédi theorem to dense sets of return times in finite orbit
segments, using an averaging argument to obtain a positive-measure family of such segments.

## Sources

- H. Furstenberg, J. Analyse Math. 31 (1977) and Recurrence in Ergodic Theory (1981); Lean states one-transformation arithmetic-progression k-term intersection form without ergodicity hypothesis.

articles.title: Measure-preserving automorphism
articles.statement:
An automorphism of a measure space $(X, m)$ is a
bijection $e \colon X \to X$ such that $e$ and its inverse are measurable and $e$ preserves $m$,
that is, $m(e^{-1}(A)) = m(A)$ for every measurable set $A \subseteq X$.

articles.title: Halmos's theorem: weak mixing is generic
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a standard Borel space and $m$ a
probability measure on $X$ for which every singleton has measure $0$. Give the set of
automorphisms of $(X, m)$ the weak topology, the topology generated by the sets of
automorphisms $T$ with $m(T(A) \mathbin{\triangle} T_0(A)) < \varepsilon$, for each automorphism
$T_0$, measurable set $A \subseteq X$ and real number $\varepsilon > 0$. Then there is a dense
$G_\delta$ set of automorphisms all of which are weakly mixing, and every weakly mixing
automorphism of $(X, m)$ is ergodic for $m$.

## Sources

- P.R. Halmos, 'In general a measure-preserving transformation is mixing', Ann. of Math. (2) 45 (1944) 786–792, and *Lectures on Ergodic Theory*, Chelsea, 1956. Related Baire-category genericity results in ergodic theory: A. Katok and A. Stepin (1967); J.R. Choksi (1965). Listed as §90 in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `halmos_generic_weak_mixing` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Weakly mixing automorphism
articles.statement:
Let $(X, m)$ be a measure space. An automorphism $T$ of
$(X, m)$ is weakly mixing if for all measurable sets $A, B \subseteq X$,

$$\frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \left| m(T^{-k}(A) \cap B) - m(A) m(B) \right| \to 0$$

as $n \to \infty$, where $T^{-k}(A)$ is the preimage of $A$ under the $k$-th iterate of $T$.

Measures are converted to real numbers here, with an infinite measure counted as $0$.

articles.title: Additive cocycle of Birkhoff sums of the first term
articles.statement: The additive cocycle `n ↦ ∑_{k<n} X 1 ∘ T^[k]` (the Birkhoff sums of `X 1`).

articles.title: Cocycle inequality holds for all indices almost everywhere
articles.statement: The cocycle inequality holds for all `m, n` simultaneously, almost everywhere.

articles.title: Subadditive cocycle bounded by Birkhoff sums of its first term
articles.statement: Iterating subadditivity: `X n ≤ ∑_{k<n} X 1 ∘ T^[k]` almost everywhere, for all `n ≥ 1`.

articles.title: Block decomposition bound for a subadditive cocycle
articles.statement: Block decomposition: `X (q k) ≤ ∑_{j<q} X k ∘ T^{j k}` almost everywhere.

articles.title: Lower limit of the normalized defect is finite almost everywhere
articles.statement: If the time constant is finite, `liminf_n Zc n / n < ∞` almost everywhere (Fatou).

articles.title: Kingman's theorem: normalized cocycle converges almost everywhere
articles.statement: If the time constant is finite, `X n / n` converges almost everywhere.

articles.title: Cost of a bad step in the greedy decomposition
articles.statement: The cost `1_{badSet} X 1` of a bad step.

articles.title: Bad set in the greedy decomposition for Kingman's theorem
articles.statement: The bad set: points where `X m x > (gLow x + ε) m` for every block length `1 ≤ m ≤ N`.

articles.title: Normalized expectations of a nonnegative cocycle are bounded below
articles.statement: For a nonnegative cocycle, `expSeq n / n` is bounded below by `0`.

articles.title: Per-step budget of the greedy decomposition
articles.statement: The per-step budget `gLow + ε + 1_{badSet} X 1` of the greedy decomposition.

articles.title: Ordered extended reals with equal real parts are equal
articles.statement: Two extended reals `x ≤ y` with `x ≠ ⊥`, `y ≠ ⊤` and equal real parts are equal.

articles.title: Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem for nonnegative cocycles
articles.statement:
Kingman's theorem for nonnegative cocycles, with integrable and invariant limit: if `T`
preserves the finite measure `μ` and `X` is a nonnegative integrable subadditive cocycle, then
`X n / n` converges a.e. to an integrable `T`-invariant function. This is
`MathlibExt.Dynamics.Ergodic.KingmanWanted.kingman_subadditive` without its hypotheses that each
`X n` is measurable and `X 0 = 0`, and for finite rather than probability measures.

articles.title: Expectation of a subadditive cocycle grows at most linearly
articles.statement: `∫ X n dμ ≤ n ∫ X 1 dμ` for `n ≥ 1`.

articles.title: Expectations of a subadditive cocycle are subadditive
articles.statement: The expectations of a subadditive cocycle are subadditive.

articles.title: Expectation sequence of a cocycle
articles.statement: The expectation `∫ X n dμ` of the `n`-th term.

articles.title: Real lower limit of a normalized cocycle
articles.statement: The lower limit `liminf_n X n x / n`, cast to `ℝ`.

articles.title: Upper and lower limits of a nonnegative cocycle agree
articles.statement: For a nonnegative cocycle the upper and lower limits of `X n / n` agree almost everywhere.

articles.title: Upper limit of a cocycle bounded by Birkhoff limits of blocks
articles.statement: For each `k ≥ 1`, `limsup X n / n ≤ birkhoffLimit (T^[k]) (X k) / k` almost everywhere.

articles.title: Lower limit of a cocycle is nondecreasing along the map
articles.statement: The lower limit is nondecreasing along `T`: `g_* ≤ g_* ∘ T` almost everywhere.

articles.title: Lower limit of a normalized subadditive cocycle
articles.statement: The lower limit `liminf_n X n x / n` in `EReal`.

articles.title: Upper limit of a normalized cocycle is finite almost everywhere
articles.statement: `limsup X n / n < ⊤` almost everywhere.

articles.title: Upper limit of a normalized subadditive cocycle
articles.statement:
The upper limit `limsup_n X n x / n` in `EReal`. The map `T` is a parameter only so that
the notation records the cocycle's base map.

articles.title: Time constant is a lower bound for normalized expectations
articles.statement: `gamma ≤ expSeq n / n` for every `n ≠ 0`.

articles.title: Time constant is at most the first expectation
articles.statement: `gamma ≤ ∫ X 1 dμ`.

articles.title: Time constant is at most the integral of the lower limit
articles.statement: The time constant is at most `∫ g_*`.

articles.title: Time constant of a subadditive cocycle
articles.statement:
The time constant `lim_n (∫ X n dμ) / n = inf_n (∫ X n dμ) / n` (Fekete's lemma); it is
meaningful when `expSeq n / n` is bounded below.

articles.title: Windowed greedy bound from time zero
articles.statement: The greedy bound from time `0`, with the remainder bounded by a sum over the last window.

articles.title: Greedy decomposition along an orbit
articles.statement:
Greedy decomposition along one orbit: `X n (T^[s] x)` is at most the sum of the budgets
`dep` over `n` steps plus one remainder term, for every `n` and starting time `s`.

articles.title: Integrability of the Kingman limit for nonnegative cocycles
articles.statement: For a nonnegative cocycle, `kingmanLimit` is integrable.

articles.title: Integral is invariant under iterates of a measure-preserving map
articles.statement:
The integral is invariant under iterates of a measure-preserving map:
`∫ g ∘ T^[m] dμ = ∫ g dμ` for a.e.-strongly measurable `g`. See also
`MathlibExt.Probability.BirkhoffErgodicL1.integral_comp_iterate_of_measurePreserving`, which
assumes `g` integrable.

articles.title: Integral is invariant under a measure-preserving map
articles.statement:
The integral is invariant under a measure-preserving map: `∫ g ∘ T dμ = ∫ g dμ` for
a.e.-strongly measurable `g`.

articles.title: Integral of the Kingman limit is at most the time constant
articles.statement: For a nonnegative cocycle, `∫ kingmanLimit ≤ gamma`.

articles.title: Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem
articles.statement:
**Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem** (J. F. C. Kingman, *The ergodic theory of
subadditive stochastic processes*, 1968): if `X` is a subadditive cocycle over a map `T`
preserving the finite measure `μ` and `inf_n (∫ X n dμ) / n > -∞`, then `X n / n` converges
`μ`-almost everywhere to the finite limit `kingmanLimit T X`. The sign of `X` is arbitrary.
Invariance and integrability of the limit, and `∫ kingmanLimit = gamma`, are not stated here; for
nonnegative cocycles see `exists_invariant_limit_of_nonneg`, which contains
`MathlibExt.Dynamics.Ergodic.KingmanWanted.kingman_subadditive`.

articles.title: Invariance of the Kingman limit
articles.statement:
Under the hypotheses of `tendsto_div_kingmanLimit_ae` and integrability of the limit, the
limit is `T`-invariant almost everywhere.

articles.title: Kingman limit of a subadditive cocycle
articles.statement:
The limit `lim X n / n` in Kingman's theorem, defined as `limsup X n / n` cast to `ℝ` (so it is
`0` where the `limsup` is infinite).

articles.title: Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem (nonnegative case)
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure
on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$. Let
$(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be functions $\alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, each measurable and
$\mu$-integrable, such that for every $n$ the inequality $f_n \ge 0$ holds $\mu$-almost
everywhere, $f_0 = 0$ holds $\mu$-almost everywhere, and for all natural numbers $m$ and $n$ the
inequality $f_{m+n}(x) \le f_m(x) + f_n(T^m x)$ holds for $\mu$-almost every $x$. Then there is a
$\mu$-integrable function $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $g(T x) = g(x)$ for $\mu$-almost
every $x$ and $f_n(x)/n$ converges to $g(x)$ as $n \to \infty$ for $\mu$-almost every $x$.

## Sources

- J. F. C. Kingman, "The Ergodic Theory of Subadditive Stochastic Processes", Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B 30 (1968), 499–510, DOI 10.1111/j.2517-6161.1968.tb00749.x.

articles.title: Dominating function for remainder terms in Kingman's theorem
articles.statement: The integrable dominating function `∑_{r<k} (X r)⁺` for the remainder terms `X r`, `r < k`.

articles.title: Shifted subadditivity defect of a cocycle
articles.statement: The shifted defect `X n + M n - addCoc n`, a subadditive cocycle for every `M`.

articles.title: Subadditive cocycle over a measure-preserving map
articles.statement:
`X` is a subadditive cocycle over `T`: `T` preserves `μ`, every `X n` is integrable, and
`X (m + n) ≤ X m + X n ∘ T^[m]` almost everywhere.

articles.title: Expectations of a subadditive cocycle form a subadditive sequence
articles.statement: The expectations of a subadditive cocycle form a `Subadditive` sequence.

articles.title: Integrable function along an orbit divided by time tends to zero
articles.statement: For integrable `g`, `g (T^[m] x) / m → 0` almost everywhere.

articles.title: Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem
articles.statement:
**Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem** for nonnegative cocycles: `X n / n` converges almost
everywhere to `kingmanLimit T X` (J. F. C. Kingman, 1968; proof of J. M. Steele, 1989).

articles.title: Almost-everywhere convergence to the Kingman limit
articles.statement:
If `g* ≤ g_*` and `g* > ⊥` almost everywhere, then `X n / n → kingmanLimit` almost
everywhere.

articles.title: Fekete's lemma for the expectations of a subadditive cocycle
articles.statement: Fekete's lemma for the expectations: `expSeq n / n → gamma` when bounded below.

articles.title: Truncated defect is a nonnegative subadditive cocycle
articles.statement: The truncated defect is a nonnegative subadditive cocycle.

articles.title: Truncated subadditivity defect of a cocycle
articles.statement: The truncated defect `(Sc M n)⁺ = (M n - Zc n)⁺`, a nonnegative subadditive cocycle.

articles.title: Negative defect is a subadditive cocycle
articles.statement: The negative defect is a subadditive cocycle.

articles.title: Negative subadditivity defect of a cocycle
articles.statement: The negative defect `X n - addCoc n` (`0` at `n = 0`), a nonpositive subadditive cocycle.

articles.title: Subadditivity defect of a cocycle
articles.statement: The subadditivity defect `addCoc n - X n` (`0` at `n = 0`); it is nonnegative a.e.

articles.title: Krylov–Bogolyubov theorem
articles.statement:
Every continuous map $T : X \to X$ of a nonempty compact metric
space $X$ to itself has an invariant Borel probability measure: there is a probability measure
$\mu$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $X$ whose pushforward under $T$ equals $\mu$.

## Sources

- N. M. Krylov and N. N. Bogolyubov, Ann. Math. 38 (1937), 65-113, DOI 10.2307/1968511.

articles.title: Coordinate shift between grid cubes
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $d$ be natural numbers, let
$\sigma$ be a permutation of the index set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}^d$, let $k$ be an index and
let $i < d$. The shift along axis $i$ determined by $\sigma$ and $k$ is the point
$(\sigma(k)_i - k_i)/n$ of the circle $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$, that is, the class modulo $1$
of this real number.

For an index $j$, the grid cube with index $j$ is the set of points of the torus
$(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^d$ whose $m$-th coordinate is the class of a real number in
$[j_m/n, (j_m + 1)/n)$ for every $m < d$. For $n > 0$, translating the $m$-th coordinate of
each point of the grid cube with index $k$ by the shift along axis $m$, for every $m < d$,
carries that cube onto the grid cube with index $\sigma(k)$.

articles.title: Grid cube in the torus
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $d$ be natural numbers and let
$k = (k_0, \dots, k_{d-1})$ with each $k_i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. The grid cube with
index $k$ is the set of points $x$ of the torus $\mathbb{T}^d = (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^d$
such that, for every $i < d$, the coordinate $x_i$ is the class modulo $1$ of some real
number $r$ with $k_i/n \le r < (k_i + 1)/n$.

articles.title: Essential-supremum distance between volume-preserving maps
articles.statement:
Let $d$ be a natural
number and let $T$ and $S$ be measurable, invertible, volume-preserving transformations of the
torus $\mathbb{T}^d = (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^d$. Let $\rho$ be the distance on $\mathbb{T}^d$
given by the maximum over the coordinates of the distance on the circle $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$
(taken to be $0$ when $d = 0$). The distance $\delta(T, S) \in [0, \infty]$ is the essential
supremum, with respect to the volume measure, of the function $x \mapsto \rho(T x, S x)$.

This is Knill's metric $\delta$.

articles.title: Cyclic cube exchange
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $d$ be natural numbers. For an index
$k \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}^d$, the grid cube with index $k$ is the set of points of the torus
$\mathbb{T}^d = (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^d$ whose $i$-th coordinate is the class of a real
number in $[k_i/n, (k_i + 1)/n)$ for every $i < d$. A measurable, invertible,
volume-preserving transformation $T$ of $\mathbb{T}^d$ is a cyclic cube exchange with $n$
subdivisions if $n > 0$ and there is a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}^d$ that is
a single cycle moving every index, such that for every index $k$, every point $x$ of the
grid cube with index $k$ and every $i < d$, we have
$(T x)_i = x_i + (\sigma(k)_i - k_i)/n$ in $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. Thus $T$ translates each
grid cube $k$ rigidly onto the grid cube $\sigma(k)$.

articles.title: Lax's approximation theorem
articles.statement:
Let $d \ge 1$ be a natural number and let $T$ be a toral
dynamical system on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d = (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^d$, regarded as a
measurable, invertible, volume-preserving transformation of $\mathbb{T}^d$. Then for every
$\varepsilon \in (0, \infty]$ there are a natural number $n$ and a measurable, invertible,
volume-preserving transformation $S$ of $\mathbb{T}^d$ such that $S$ is a cyclic cube exchange
with $n$ subdivisions and $\delta(T, S) < \varepsilon$, where $\delta$ is the
essential-supremum distance between volume-preserving maps.

## Sources

- P. D. Lax, *Approximation of measure preserving transformations*, Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 24 (1971). Knill, *Some fundamental theorems in mathematics*, §110. Problem `lax_approximation` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Toral dynamical systems as volume-preserving transformations
articles.statement:
Let $d$ be a natural
number. A volume-preserving homeomorphism $T$ of the torus
$\mathbb{T}^d = (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^d$ is regarded as a measurable, invertible,
volume-preserving transformation of $\mathbb{T}^d$: the same map, with its inverse, viewed as
a measurable equivalence.

articles.title: Toral dynamical system
articles.statement:
Let $d$ be a natural number. A toral dynamical system on the
torus $\mathbb{T}^d = (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^d$ is a homeomorphism of $\mathbb{T}^d$ that
preserves the volume measure.

articles.title: Torus
articles.statement:
For a natural number $d$, the $d$-dimensional torus is
$\mathbb{T}^d = (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^d$, the product of $d$ copies of the circle
$\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$.

articles.title: Volume-preserving transformations of the torus
articles.statement:
Let $d$ be a natural number. A
volume-preserving transformation of the torus $\mathbb{T}^d = (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^d$ is a
bijection $T$ of $\mathbb{T}^d$ such that $T$ and $T^{-1}$ are measurable and $T$ preserves
the volume measure.

articles.title: Multiplicative recurrence along Pythagorean pairs
articles.statement:
Let $(X, \mu)$ be a probability space
and let $(T_a)_{a \ge 1}$, indexed by the positive integers, be measurable bijections of $X$ with
measurable inverses that preserve $\mu$, such that $T_1$ is the identity and
$T_{ab} = T_a \circ T_b$ for all positive integers $a, b$. Then for every measurable set
$A \subseteq X$ with $\mu(A) > 0$ there exist positive integers $m > n$ such that

$$\mu\bigl(T_{2mn}(A) \cap T_{(m-n)(m+n)}(A)\bigr) > 0.$$

Resolved true: Resolved by Frantzikinakis-Klurman-Moreira, Partition Regularity of Pythagorean
Pairs (arXiv:2309.10636), Theorem 2.1(i): applied with coefficients 1 and 2 to the inverse
family, it yields the two forward-image indices of AMR-047-0034. The statement is retained as a
resolved target. Source: Frantzikinakis, Klurman, Moreira, Partition Regularity of Pythagorean
Pairs, arXiv:2309.10636, Theorem 2.1(i), https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.10636. Moved from
`OpenConjectures/Dynamics/MultStructureRecurrence`.

articles.title: Pythagorean-pair recurrence problem (AMR-047-0034)
articles.statement:
The proposition that for every
probability space $(X, \mu)$ and every family $(T_a)_{a \ge 1}$, indexed by the positive integers,
of measurable bijections of $X$ with measurable inverses that preserve $\mu$, such that $T_1$ is
the identity and $T_{ab} = T_a \circ T_b$ for all positive integers $a, b$, every measurable set
$A \subseteq X$ with $\mu(A) > 0$ admits positive integers $m > n$ with

$$\mu\bigl(T_{2mn}(A) \cap T_{(m-n)(m+n)}(A)\bigr) > 0.$$

articles.title: Integer box
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $d$ and $N$, the integer box $[0, N)^d$ is the finite set
of vectors $v \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ with $0 \le v_i < N$ for every coordinate $i$.

articles.title: Aperiodic transformation
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\Omega$. A map
$T : \Omega \to \Omega$ is aperiodic with respect to $\mu$ if the set of periodic points of $T$,
the points $x$ with $T^k(x) = x$ for some $k \ge 1$, where $T^k$ is the $k$-fold iterate of $T$,
has (outer) $\mu$-measure zero. Equivalently, for $\mu$-almost every $x$, no positive iterate of
$T$ fixes $x$.

articles.title: Free $\mathbb{Z}^d$-action
articles.statement:
Let $d$ be a natural number, let $\mu$ be a measure on a
measurable space $\Omega$, and let $T$ assign to each $v \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ a map
$T_v \colon \Omega \to \Omega$. Then $T$ is free (in the Ornstein–Weiss sense) with respect to
$\mu$ if, for every nonzero $v \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, the set of points $x \in \Omega$ with
$T_v(x) = x$ has $\mu$-measure zero.

articles.title: Rokhlin tower
articles.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a measurable space, $T : \Omega \to \Omega$ a map and
$n \in \mathbb{N}$. A set $B \subseteq \Omega$ is the base of a Rokhlin tower of height $n$
for $T$ if $B$ is measurable and the floors $B, T(B), \dots, T^{n-1}(B)$ are pairwise
disjoint, that is, $T^i(B) \cap T^j(B) = \emptyset$ for all $i \ne j$ with $i, j < n$; here
$T^k(B)$ is the image of $B$ under the $k$-fold iterate of $T$.

Only the base is required to be measurable. For a non-invertible $T$, the floors need not be
measurable, so evaluating a measure on their union uses its outer measure.

articles.title: Ornstein–Weiss Rokhlin lemma for $\mathbb{Z}^d$-actions
articles.statement:
Let $d \ge 1$, let $\Omega$ be a
standard Borel space with a probability measure $\mu$, and let $T$ assign to each
$v \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ a map $T_v \colon \Omega \to \Omega$ such that $T_0$ is the identity,
$T_{u + v} = T_u \circ T_v$ for all $u, v \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, every $T_v$ is measure preserving
for $\mu$, and the action is free (for every $v \ne 0$ the set of fixed points of $T_v$ has
$\mu$-measure zero). Then for every integer $N \ge 1$ and every $\varepsilon \in (0, \infty]$
there is a measurable set $B \subseteq \Omega$ such that the images $T_v(B)$, for $v$ in the
integer box $[0, N)^d$, are pairwise disjoint and their union has measure at least
$1 - \varepsilon$.

## Sources

- D. S. Ornstein and B. Weiss, *Entropy and isomorphism theorems for actions of amenable groups*, J. Anal. Math. 48 (1987), 1-141 — Theorem 5.2 establishes the multidimensional (and amenable-group) Rokhlin lemma. Listed as §109 in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). No formalization found in any major prover. Problem `ornstein_weiss_rokhlin` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Rokhlin lemma for non-invertible maps
articles.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a standard Borel space with a
probability measure $\mu$, and let $T : \Omega \to \Omega$ be a measure-preserving map that is
aperiodic with respect to $\mu$. Then for every integer $n \ge 1$ and every
$\varepsilon \in (0, \infty]$ there is a measurable set $B \subseteq \Omega$ such that the
floors $B, T(B), \dots, T^{n-1}(B)$ are pairwise disjoint, where $T^k(B)$ is the image of $B$
under the $k$-fold iterate of $T$, and their union $\bigcup_{k=0}^{n-1} T^k(B)$ has outer
$\mu$-measure at least $1 - \varepsilon$ (truncated subtraction, so the bound is $0$ when
$\varepsilon \ge 1$). No invertibility of $T$ is assumed.

## Sources

- V. A. Rokhlin, *A general measure-preserving transformation is not mixing*, Doklady Akademii Nauk SSSR 60 (1948), 349-351 (original Russian; English translation later); S. Kakutani, *Induced measure-preserving transformations*, Proc. Imp. Acad. Tokyo 19 (1943), 635-641 (independent discovery); S.-M. Heinemann and O. Schmitt, *Rokhlin's lemma for non-invertible maps*, Dynam. Systems Appl. 10 (2001), no. 2, 201-213. The classical form is listed as §109 in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `rokhlin_lemma` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Floor of a Rokhlin tower
articles.statement:
For a map $T : \Omega \to \Omega$, a set
$B \subseteq \Omega$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the level-$k$ floor with base $B$ is the image
$T^k(B)$ of $B$ under the $k$-fold iterate $T^k$ of $T$; the level-$0$ floor is $B$.

articles.title: Union of a Rokhlin tower
articles.statement:
For a map $T : \Omega \to \Omega$, a set
$B \subseteq \Omega$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the union of the tower with base $B$ and height $n$
is the set $\bigcup_{k=0}^{n-1} T^k(B)$ of its floors $B, T(B), \dots, T^{n-1}(B)$, where
$T^k(B)$ is the image of $B$ under the $k$-fold iterate of $T$. It is empty when $n = 0$, and
no disjointness of the floors is required.

articles.title: Li–Yorke theorem: period three implies all periods
articles.statement:
Let $f \colon [0, 1] \to [0, 1]$ be a
continuous map. If some point of $[0, 1]$ has minimal period $3$ under $f$, then for every
positive integer $n$ some point of $[0, 1]$ has minimal period $n$ under $f$.

## Sources

- T.-Y. Li and J. A. Yorke, Period Three Implies Chaos, Amer. Math. Monthly 82 (1975), 985-992, DOI 10.2307/2318254.

articles.title: Real-analytic circle diffeomorphisms
articles.statement:
A real-analytic orientation-preserving
diffeomorphism of the circle is given by a lift $F : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ together with an
inverse lift $G : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, both real-analytic on all of $\mathbb{R}$, such that
for every real $x$ we have $F(x + 1) = F(x) + 1$, $G(x + 1) = G(x) + 1$, $G(F(x)) = x$ and
$F(G(x)) = x$, and $F$ is strictly increasing.

## Sources

- Hayman (2018), Problem 2.90; https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200.

articles.title: Herman's analytic linearization problem has a positive answer
articles.statement:
There is an irrational real
number $\alpha$ that is not Diophantine such that, for every real-analytic circle diffeomorphism
whose lift $F$ has rotation number $\alpha$, $F$ is analytically conjugate to the rotation by
$\alpha$.

Yoccoz characterized the Herman class $\mathcal{H}$ of rotation numbers $\alpha$ for which every
real-analytic circle diffeomorphism with rotation number $\alpha$ is analytically linearizable,
and proved that $\mathcal{H}$ strictly contains the set of Diophantine numbers; any $\alpha$ in
$\mathcal{H}$ that is not Diophantine has the required property.

## Sources

- H. Eliasson, B. Fayad and R. Krikorian, Jean-Christophe Yoccoz and the theory of circle diffeomorphisms (2018), arXiv:1810.07107 (account of J.-C. Yoccoz, Analytic linearization of circle diffeomorphisms, Lecture Notes in Math. 1784, Springer (2002), 125-173), https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.07107.

articles.title: Herman's analytic linearization problem
articles.statement:
The statement that there is an irrational real
number $\alpha$ that is not Diophantine such that, for every real-analytic circle diffeomorphism
whose lift $F$ has rotation number $\alpha$, $F$ is analytically conjugate to the rotation by
$\alpha$.

M. R. Herman asked whether such an $\alpha$ exists; this is Problem 2.90 in Hayman's list.

## Sources

- Hayman (2018), Problem 2.90; https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200.

articles.title: Rotation number of a lift
articles.statement:
Let $F : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function, and for a
natural number $n$ write $F^n$ for the $n$-th iterate of $F$. Then $F$ has rotation number
$\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ when, for every real $x$, $(F^n(x) - x)/n$ tends to $\alpha$ as $n$ tends
to infinity.

## Sources

- Hayman (2018), Problem 2.90; https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200.

articles.title: Analytic conjugacy to a rotation
articles.statement:
A function $F : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is
analytically conjugate to the rotation by $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ when there is a real-analytic
circle diffeomorphism with lift $H$ such that $H(F(x)) = H(x) + \alpha$ for every real $x$.

## Sources

- Hayman (2018), Problem 2.90; https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200.

articles.title: Diophantine numbers
articles.statement:
A real number $\alpha$ is Diophantine when there are real numbers
$\gamma > 0$ and $\tau \ge 0$ such that $|\alpha - p/q| \ge \gamma / q^{2 + \tau}$ for every
integer $p$ and every integer $q \ge 1$.

## Sources

- Hayman (2018), Problem 2.90; https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200.

articles.title: Block counts of the ideal period words
articles.statement:
For every $n \ge 1$, the ideal period word $d_n$
contains exactly $2^{n-1}$ blocks $2, 2$, and the number $c_n$ of its blocks $2, 1, 1$ satisfies
$3 c_n = 2^n - (-1)^n$; that is, $c_n = (2^n + 1)/3$ for odd $n$ and $c_n = (2^n - 1)/3$ for even
$n$.

In this lemma the source names the blocks $a = 2, 2$ and $b = 2, 1, 1$, the reverse of its
Definition 7; the counts are stated by block, so the naming does not matter.

## Sources

- Jaap de Jonge, *Intervals of N-Expansions with Many Gaps*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A75, Lemma 8.

articles.title: The fifth ideal period word
articles.statement:
Writing $a$ for the block $2, 1, 1$ and $b$ for the block
$2, 2$ of partial quotients, the ideal period word $d_5$ is $d_4$ followed by the blocks
$abb\,ab\,ab\,abb\,ab\,ab$, in this order.

This is the second recursion rule applied to $d_4 = [j, abb]$ with $j = [abb, ab, ab, abb]$.

## Sources

- Jaap de Jonge, *Intervals of N-Expansions with Many Gaps*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A75, Definition 7.

articles.title: Lengths of the first ideal period words
articles.statement:
The digit strings of the ideal period words
$d_1, d_2, d_3, d_4, d_5$ have lengths $5, 7, 17, 31, 65$ respectively.

## Sources

- Jaap de Jonge, *Intervals of N-Expansions with Many Gaps*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A75, Definition 7.

articles.title: Length of the ideal period words
articles.statement:
For every $n \ge 1$, the digit string of the ideal
period word $d_n$ (the concatenation of its blocks of partial quotients) has length
$|d_n| = 2^{n+1} - (-1)^n$.

The source derives this from the recursion $|d_n| = 2|d_{n-1}| - 3(-1)^n$.

## Sources

- Jaap de Jonge, *Intervals of N-Expansions with Many Gaps*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A75, Lemma 7.

articles.title: The ideal periodic point is the least point of its orbit
articles.statement:
Let $N$ be a natural number,
let $\alpha$ be a real number with $0 < \alpha \le \sqrt N - 1$, and let $T_\alpha$ be the
$N$-expansion map on $I_\alpha = [\alpha, \alpha + 1]$. Let $n \ge 1$, write $|d_n|$ for the
length of the digit string of the ideal period word $d_n$, and let $x \in I_\alpha$ be such that
for every $i \ge 0$ the digit of $T_\alpha^i(x)$ is entry $i \bmod |d_n|$ (counting from $0$) of
that digit string, so that the expansion of $x$ is purely periodic with period word $d_n$. Then
$x \le T_\alpha^j(x)$ for every $j \ge 0$.

The source assumes Phase I; only the assumption $0 < \alpha \le \sqrt N - 1$ is kept here.

## Sources

- Jaap de Jonge, *Intervals of N-Expansions with Many Gaps*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A75, Lemma 5.

articles.title: The ideal periodic points decrease
articles.statement:
Let $N$ be a natural number, let $\alpha$ be a real
number with $0 < \alpha \le \sqrt N - 1$, and let $T_\alpha$ be the $N$-expansion map on
$I_\alpha = [\alpha, \alpha + 1]$. For $m \ge 1$ write $|d_m|$ for the length of the digit string
of the ideal period word $d_m$. Let $k, \ell \ge 1$ and let $x, y \in I_\alpha$ be such that for
every $i \ge 0$ the digit of $T_\alpha^i(x)$ is entry $i \bmod |d_k|$ (counting from $0$) of the
digit string of $d_k$, and the digit of $T_\alpha^i(y)$ is entry $i \bmod |d_\ell|$ of the digit
string of $d_\ell$; that is, the expansions of $x$ and $y$ are purely periodic with period words
$d_k$ and $d_\ell$. Then $x < y$ if and only if $\ell < k$.

The source works in Phase I; only the assumption $0 < \alpha \le \sqrt N - 1$ is kept here, which
makes $T_\alpha$ expanding, so that a digit sequence determines its point.

## Sources

- Jaap de Jonge, *Intervals of N-Expansions with Many Gaps*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A75, Lemma 4.

articles.title: Ideal period words
articles.statement:
For $n \ge 1$, the ideal period word $d_n$ is a finite list of blocks
of partial quotients, each block being $a = 2, 1, 1$ or $b = 2, 2$. Writing lists of blocks by
juxtaposition, with commas between parts, $d_1 = [ab]$, $d_2 = [abb]$, $d_3 = [abb, ab, ab]$ and
$d_4 = [abb, ab, ab, abb, abb]$; for $n \ge 5$, if $d_{n-1} = [j, ab, ab]$ for a list $j$ then
$d_n = [j, ab, ab, j, abb]$, and if $d_{n-1} = [j, abb]$ then $d_n = [j, abb, j, ab, ab]$. The
digit string of $d_n$ is the concatenation of its blocks. For $n = 0$ the list is empty, a
placeholder.

## Sources

- Jaap de Jonge, *Intervals of N-Expansions with Many Gaps*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A75, Definition 7.

articles.title: The digit away from the left endpoint
articles.statement:
Let $N$ be a natural number and let $\alpha$ and
$x$ be real numbers with $x \ne \alpha$. Then the digit of $x$ for the $N$-expansion map on
$[\alpha, \alpha + 1]$ is $\lfloor N/x - \alpha \rfloor$.

## Sources

- Jaap de Jonge, *Intervals of N-Expansions with Many Gaps*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A75, Definition 1.

articles.title: Digit of the N-expansion map
articles.statement:
Let $N$ be a natural number and $\alpha$ a real number, and
write $I_\alpha = [\alpha, \alpha + 1]$. The digit of a real number $x$ is
$d(x) = \lfloor N/x - \alpha \rfloor$, except that when $N/\alpha - \alpha$ is an integer, the
digit of $\alpha$ itself is $d(\alpha) = N/\alpha - \alpha - 1$.

With this choice the $N$-expansion map $T_\alpha(x) = N/x - d(x)$ sends $\alpha$ to $\alpha + 1$
in the integer case, every other point of $I_\alpha$ lands in $[\alpha, \alpha + 1)$, and no
cylinder is a single point.

## Sources

- Jaap de Jonge, *Intervals of N-Expansions with Many Gaps*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A75, Definition 1.

articles.title: The N-expansion map away from the left endpoint
articles.statement:
Let $N$ be a natural number and let
$\alpha$ and $x$ be real numbers with $x \ne \alpha$. Then the $N$-expansion map $T_\alpha$
satisfies $\alpha \le T_\alpha(x) < \alpha + 1$.

Indeed $T_\alpha(x) = \alpha + \{N/x - \alpha\}$, where $\{\cdot\}$ denotes the fractional part.

## Sources

- Jaap de Jonge, *Intervals of N-Expansions with Many Gaps*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A75, Definition 1.

articles.title: The left endpoint goes to the right endpoint when $N/\alpha - \alpha$ is an integer
articles.statement:
Let
$N$ be a natural number and $\alpha$ a real number such that $N/\alpha - \alpha$ is an integer,
with the convention $N/0 = 0$. Then the $N$-expansion map $T_\alpha$ satisfies
$T_\alpha(\alpha) = \alpha + 1$.

## Sources

- Jaap de Jonge, *Intervals of N-Expansions with Many Gaps*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A75, Definition 1.

articles.title: The $N$-expansion map
articles.statement:
For a natural number $N$ and a real number $\alpha$, the
$N$-expansion map is $T_\alpha(x) = N/x - d_\alpha(x)$ for real $x$, where $d_\alpha(x)$ is the
$N$-expansion digit: $d_\alpha(x) = \lfloor N/x - \alpha \rfloor$, except that
$d_\alpha(\alpha) = \lfloor N/\alpha - \alpha \rfloor - 1$ when $N/\alpha - \alpha$ is an integer.
The map is meant to act on the interval $I_\alpha = [\alpha, \alpha + 1]$, but it is defined for
every real $x$, with the convention $N/0 = 0$.

## Sources

- Jaap de Jonge, *Intervals of N-Expansions with Many Gaps*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A75, Definition 1.

articles.title: Orbits with the same digits alternate in order
articles.statement:
Let $N$ be a positive integer and let
$0 < \alpha < \alpha'$ be real numbers. Write $T_\alpha$ for the $N$-expansion map and $d_\alpha$
for the $N$-expansion digit with parameter $\alpha$, and let $m$ be a natural number. If the
orbits $\alpha_j = T_\alpha^j(\alpha)$ and $\alpha'_j = T_{\alpha'}^j(\alpha')$ satisfy
$d_\alpha(\alpha_j) = d_{\alpha'}(\alpha'_j)$ for all $j \in \{0, \dots, m\}$, then
$\alpha'_m < \alpha_m$ if and only if $m$ is odd. Likewise, if the orbits
$\beta_j = T_\alpha^j(\alpha + 1)$ and $\beta'_j = T_{\alpha'}^j(\alpha' + 1)$ satisfy
$d_\alpha(\beta_j) = d_{\alpha'}(\beta'_j)$ for all $j \in \{0, \dots, m\}$, then
$\beta'_m < \beta_m$ if and only if $m$ is odd.

The paper assumes $\alpha$ and $\alpha'$ in Phase I (so in particular $\alpha' \le \sqrt N - 1$);
for $N > 0$ neither assumption is needed (the orbits stay in $[\alpha, \alpha + 1]$ and
$[\alpha', \alpha' + 1]$, where $x \mapsto N/x$ is strictly decreasing), so both are replaced by
$N > 0$. For $N = 0$ the claim fails ($\alpha = 1/5$, $\alpha' = 3/10$, $m = 1$).

## Sources

- Jaap de Jonge, *Intervals of N-Expansions with Many Gaps*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A75, Lemma 2.

articles.title: Central equations for natural duals of Moebius maps
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$
and $\xi$ be real numbers with $\alpha > 0$, $\beta < 1$, $\gamma > -1$ and $\delta \ge 0$. Define
the dual branches
$V^\#_{\alpha\gamma}(y) = (\gamma - 2\alpha - \alpha y)/(2\alpha + 1 + \alpha y)$,
$V^\#_{\alpha\delta}(y) = (2\alpha\delta - 1 + \alpha\delta y)/(2\alpha + 1 + \alpha y)$,
$V^\#_{\beta\gamma}(y) = (2\beta + \gamma - 2 + (\beta + \gamma - 1) y)/
(3 - 2\beta + (2 - \beta) y)$ and
$V^\#_{\beta\delta}(y) = (2\delta - 2\beta\delta - 1 + (\delta - \beta\delta - 1) y)/
(3 - 2\beta + (2 - \beta) y)$, and put $\eta = (-2 + 2\beta + \gamma)/(2 - \beta)$. Suppose that
$3 - 2\beta + (2 - \beta)\xi \ne 0$, $2\alpha + 1 + \alpha\xi \ne 0$,
$V^\#_{\beta\gamma}(\xi) = V^\#_{\beta\delta}(\xi)$ and
$V^\#_{\alpha\delta}(\xi) = V^\#_{\alpha\gamma}(\xi)$. Then
$\alpha + \alpha\delta + \delta = \beta + \gamma + \beta\delta$; and if moreover
$2\alpha + 1 + \alpha\eta \ne 0$ and $\xi = V^\#_{\alpha\gamma}(\eta)$, then
$\alpha^2\gamma + \alpha^2\gamma\delta + 2\alpha + \beta + \beta\gamma + 2\alpha^2 +
2\alpha^2\delta + 4\alpha\delta + 2\alpha\gamma\delta = 2 + \alpha\gamma^2 + 2\gamma +
2\alpha\beta + \alpha\gamma + \alpha\beta\gamma + \alpha\beta\gamma\delta + 2\alpha\beta\delta$.

## Sources

- Fritz Schweiger, *A Remark on Singular Duals of Moebius Maps*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A17, Lemma 3.

articles.title: Moebius dual branches disagree at −1
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha, \beta, \delta$ be real numbers with
$\alpha > 0$, $\beta < 1$ and $\delta \ge 0$, and define the dual branches
$V^\#_{\alpha\delta}(y) = (2\alpha\delta - 1 + \alpha\delta y)/(2\alpha + 1 + \alpha y)$ and
$V^\#_{\beta\delta}(y) = (2\delta - 2\beta\delta - 1 + (\delta - \beta\delta - 1) y)/
(3 - 2\beta + (2 - \beta) y)$. Then $V^\#_{\beta\delta}(-1) \ne V^\#_{\alpha\delta}(-1)$.

Equality would force $\delta = -1$.

## Sources

- Fritz Schweiger, *A Remark on Singular Duals of Moebius Maps*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A17, Lemma 2.

articles.title: Fixed points of a Moebius dual branch
articles.statement:
Let $\beta, \gamma, \eta$ be real numbers with
$\beta \ne 2$ and $3 - 2\beta + (2 - \beta)\eta \ne 0$. Then
$(-2 + 2\beta + \gamma + (-1 + \beta + \gamma)\eta)/(3 - 2\beta + (2 - \beta)\eta) = \eta$
if and only if $\eta = -1$ or $\eta = (-2 + 2\beta + \gamma)/(2 - \beta)$.

The paper's further side conditions on $\beta$ and $\gamma$ are not used.

## Sources

- Fritz Schweiger, *A Remark on Singular Duals of Moebius Maps*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A17, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Singularity of natural duals of Moebius maps (algebraic form)
articles.statement:
Let
$\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ be real numbers with $\alpha > 0$, $\beta < 1$, $\gamma > -1$ and
$\delta \ge 0$. Define the dual branches
$V^\#_{\alpha\gamma}(y) = (\gamma - 2\alpha - \alpha y)/(2\alpha + 1 + \alpha y)$,
$V^\#_{\alpha\delta}(y) = (2\alpha\delta - 1 + \alpha\delta y)/(2\alpha + 1 + \alpha y)$,
$V^\#_{\beta\gamma}(y) = (2\beta + \gamma - 2 + (\beta + \gamma - 1) y)/
(3 - 2\beta + (2 - \beta) y)$ and
$V^\#_{\beta\delta}(y) = (2\delta - 2\beta\delta - 1 + (\delta - \beta\delta - 1) y)/
(3 - 2\beta + (2 - \beta) y)$, and put $\eta = (-2 + 2\beta + \gamma)/(2 - \beta)$ and
$\xi = V^\#_{\alpha\gamma}(\eta)$. If $2\alpha + 1 + \alpha\eta \ne 0$,
$3 - 2\beta + (2 - \beta)\xi \ne 0$, $2\alpha + 1 + \alpha\xi \ne 0$,
$V^\#_{\beta\gamma}(\xi) = V^\#_{\beta\delta}(\xi)$ and
$V^\#_{\alpha\delta}(\xi) = V^\#_{\alpha\gamma}(\xi)$, then $\xi = \eta$.

Here $\eta$ is a fixed point of $V^\#_{\beta\gamma}$, and $\xi = \eta$ says that the natural dual
$[\eta, \xi]$ reduces to a single point.

## Sources

- Fritz Schweiger, *A Remark on Singular Duals of Moebius Maps*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A17, Theorem 1.

articles.title: The Euclidean plane
articles.statement:
The ambient space is the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ with its Euclidean
inner product and norm.

articles.title: Poincaré–Bendixson theorem
articles.statement:
Let $F \colon \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ be a continuously
differentiable vector field on the Euclidean plane, and let
$\gamma \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^2$ be a curve such that for every $t \ge 0$ the derivative
of $\gamma$ at $t$ within $[0, \infty)$ is $F(\gamma(t))$. Let
$\omega(\gamma) = \bigcap_{s \in \mathbb{R}} \overline{\gamma([s, \infty))}$ be the $\omega$-limit
set of $\gamma$. Then at least one of the following holds: the forward orbit
$\gamma([0, \infty))$ is unbounded; $\omega(\gamma)$ contains a point $x_0$ with $F(x_0) = 0$; or
there are a real number $T > 0$ and a curve $\beta \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^2$ with
$\beta'(t) = F(\beta(t))$ and $\beta(t + T) = \beta(t)$ for every real $t$ and with
$F(\beta(0)) \ne 0$, such that $\omega(\gamma)$ equals the range of $\beta$.

## Sources

- H. Poincaré, *Mémoire sur les courbes définies par une équation différentielle*, Journal de Mathématiques 7 (1881), 8 (1882), 1 (1885), 2 (1886); I. Bendixson, *Sur les courbes définies par des équations différentielles*, Acta Mathematica 24 (1901), 1-88. Listed as §63 in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). The Isabelle/HOL/AFP entry by Fabian Immler and Yong Kiam Tan (https://www.isa-afp.org/entries/Poincare_Bendixson.html) uses John Harrison's Jordan curve theorem. Problem `poincare_bendixson` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Area-preserving homeomorphisms of the disc supported in the interior
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{D}$ be
the closed unit disc in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and let $\omega$ be the restriction of Lebesgue measure to
$\mathbb{D}$. $\mathrm{Homeo}_c(\mathbb{D}, \omega)$ is the subgroup of the group of
homeomorphisms of $\mathbb{D}$ consisting of the homeomorphisms $\phi$ that preserve $\omega$ and
whose support, the closure of $\{x \in \mathbb{D} : \phi(x) \neq x\}$, is contained in the open
unit disc.

articles.title: Simplicity conjecture
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{D} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be the closed unit disc and let
$\omega$ be the restriction of Lebesgue measure to $\mathbb{D}$. The group
$\mathrm{Homeo}_c(\mathbb{D}, \omega)$ of homeomorphisms of $\mathbb{D}$ that preserve $\omega$
and whose support, the closure of the set of non-fixed points, lies in the open unit disc is not
simple: it is trivial or it has a normal subgroup other than the trivial subgroup and the whole
group.

## Sources

- D. Cristofaro-Gardiner, V. Humilière, and S. Seyfaddini, `Proof of the simplicity conjecture`, Annals of Math, 199 (1) 2024. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_simplicity_conjecture` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Hausdorff dimension of a measure
articles.statement:
For a measure $\mu$ on an extended metric space $M$
equipped with a σ-algebra, the Hausdorff dimension of $\mu$ is the infimum, in $[0, \infty]$, of
the Hausdorff dimensions of the measurable sets $s \subseteq M$ with $\mu(M \setminus s) = 0$.

articles.title: Young's entropy–dimension–Lyapunov formula (planar case)
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a $C^2$
diffeomorphism of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$: $T$ has a two-sided inverse $T^{-1}$ and
both $T$ and $T^{-1}$ are $C^2$. Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a compact set with
$T(K) = K$, and let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with
$\mu(\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus K) = 0$ that is $T$-invariant and ergodic for $T$. Let $\lambda_1$
and $\lambda_2$ be the $\mu$-integrals of the upper and the lower Lyapunov exponent of $T$. Then
the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy of $T$ with respect to $\mu$ is

$$h_\mu(T) = \frac{\dim(\mu) \cdot H}{2},$$

where $\dim(\mu)$ is the Hausdorff dimension of $\mu$ and
$H = \frac{2 \lambda_1 (-\lambda_2)}{\lambda_1 - \lambda_2}$ is the harmonic mean of $\lambda_1$
and $-\lambda_2$, taken to be $0$ when $\lambda_1 = \lambda_2$.

## Sources

- L.-S. Young, *Dimension, entropy and Lyapunov exponents*, Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems 2 (1982), 109–124. Knill, *Some fundamental theorems in mathematics*, §103. Problem `entropy_dimension_lyapunov` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Entropy of a map relative to a partition
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space
$M$, let $T : M \to M$ be a map and let $P$ be a finite family of subsets of $M$. The entropy of
$T$ relative to $P$ is

$$h_\mu(T, P) = \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n} H_\mu\Big(\bigvee_{k=0}^{n-1} T^{-k} P\Big),$$

where $\bigvee_{k=0}^{n-1} T^{-k} P$ is the iterated join of $P$ under $T$; the Shannon entropy
of a finite family $Q$ of sets is $H_\mu(Q) = \sum_{A \in Q} -\mu(A) \log \mu(A)$, with
$0 \log 0 = 0$ and with $\mu(A)$ replaced by $0$ when $\mu(A) = \infty$; and the limit superior
is taken to be $0$ when it is $+\infty$ or $-\infty$.

articles.title: Euclidean plane
articles.statement:
The Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ with its Euclidean inner product and
norm. The theorems of this module model a compact surface by a compact invariant subset of
this plane.

articles.title: Harmonic mean of Lyapunov exponents
articles.statement:
For real numbers $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$, this
is the harmonic mean $\frac{2 \lambda_1 (-\lambda_2)}{\lambda_1 - \lambda_2}$ of $\lambda_1$ and
$-\lambda_2$, taken to be $0$ when $\lambda_1 = \lambda_2$.

articles.title: Measurable partition modulo null sets
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $M$.
A finite family $P$ of subsets of $M$ is a measurable partition of $M$ modulo $\mu$-null sets
when every member of $P$ is measurable, the complement of the union of the members of $P$ has
$\mu$-measure $0$, and any two distinct members $A \ne B$ of $P$ satisfy $\mu(A \cap B) = 0$.

articles.title: Iterated join of a partition
articles.statement:
For a map $T : M \to M$, a finite family $P$ of subsets of
$M$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the iterated join $\bigvee_{k=0}^{n-1} T^{-k} P$ is the finite family
of all sets $\bigcap_{k=0}^{n-1} T^{-k}(A_k)$ with $A_0, \dots, A_{n-1} \in P$, where $T^{-k}(A)$
is the preimage of $A$ under the $k$-th iterate $T^k$. For $n = 0$ it is $\{M\}$.

articles.title: Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy
articles.statement:
