Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $M$ and let
$T : M \to M$ be a map. The Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy $h_\mu(T)$ is the supremum of the
entropies $h_\mu(T, P)$ of $T$ relative to $P$ over all finite measurable partitions $P$ of $M$
modulo $\mu$-null sets, taken to be $0$ when these entropies are not bounded above.

articles.title: Lower Lyapunov exponent
articles.statement:
For a map $T : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ of the Euclidean
plane and a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^2$, the lower Lyapunov exponent of $T$ at $x$ is

$$\underline{\lambda}(T, x) = -\limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n} \log \|(D(T^n)_x)^{-1}\|,$$

where $D(T^n)_x$ is the derivative at $x$ of the $n$-th iterate $T^n$, taken to be $0$ when
$T^n$ is not differentiable at $x$; the inverse $(D(T^n)_x)^{-1}$ is taken to be $0$ when
$D(T^n)_x$ is not invertible; $\|\cdot\|$ is the operator norm; $\log 0 = 0$; and the limit
superior is taken to be $0$ when it is $+\infty$ or $-\infty$.

articles.title: Upper Lyapunov exponent
articles.statement:
For a map $T : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ of the Euclidean
plane and a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^2$, the upper Lyapunov exponent of $T$ at $x$ is

$$\overline{\lambda}(T, x) = \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n} \log \|D(T^n)_x\|,$$

where $D(T^n)_x$ is the derivative at $x$ of the $n$-th iterate $T^n$, taken to be $0$ when
$T^n$ is not differentiable at $x$; $\|\cdot\|$ is the operator norm; $\log 0 = 0$; and the
limit superior is taken to be $0$ when it is $+\infty$ or $-\infty$.

articles.title: Margulis–Ruelle inequality (planar case)
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a $C^2$ diffeomorphism of the
Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, that is, a $C^2$ map with a $C^2$ two-sided inverse. Let
$K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a compact set with $T(K) = K$, and let $\mu$ be an ergodic
$T$-invariant Borel probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with
$\mu(\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus K) = 0$. Write $h_\mu(T)$ for the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy of $T$
with respect to $\mu$, and $\lambda_1(x)$ and $\lambda_2(x)$ for the upper and lower Lyapunov
exponents of $T$ at $x$. Then

$$h_\mu(T) \le \max(0, \int \lambda_1 \, d\mu) + \max(0, \int \lambda_2 \, d\mu).$$

## Sources

- D. Ruelle, *An inequality for the entropy of differentiable maps*, Bol. Soc. Brasil. Mat. 9 (1978); G. A. Margulis (1968, unpublished). Knill, *Some fundamental theorems in mathematics*, §103. Problem `margulis_ruelle` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Shannon entropy of a finite family of sets
articles.statement:
For a measure $\mu$ on a measurable space $M$
and a finite collection $P$ of subsets of $M$, the entropy of $P$ is
$H_\mu(P) = \sum_{A \in P} -\mu(A) \log \mu(A)$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm, with the
convention $0 \log 0 = 0$. Here $\mu(A)$ is taken as a real number, so a set of infinite measure
contributes $0$.

It is applied to finite measurable partitions $P$.

articles.title: Pesin entropy formula (planar case)
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a $C^2$ diffeomorphism of the Euclidean
plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, that is, a $C^2$ map with a $C^2$ two-sided inverse. Let
$K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a compact set with $T(K) = K$, and let $\mu$ be an ergodic
$T$-invariant Borel probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with
$\mu(\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus K) = 0$. Write $h_\mu(T)$ for the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy of $T$
with respect to $\mu$, and $\lambda_1(x)$ and $\lambda_2(x)$ for the upper and lower Lyapunov
exponents of $T$ at $x$. Suppose that the Hausdorff dimension of $\mu$ equals $2$ and that
$\int \lambda_1 \, d\mu = -\int \lambda_2 \, d\mu$. Then $h_\mu(T) = \int \lambda_1 \, d\mu$.

## Sources

- Ya. B. Pesin, *Characteristic Lyapunov exponents and smooth ergodic theory*, Russian Math. Surveys 32 (1977). Knill, *Some fundamental theorems in mathematics*, §103. Problem `pesin_formula` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Diophantine number
articles.statement:
A real number $\alpha$ is Diophantine (with exponent $2$, as used in
KAM theory) if there is $C > 0$ such that $C / q^2 \le |\alpha - p/q|$ for all integers $p$ and
$q$ with $q \neq 0$.

articles.title: KAM theorem for twist maps (persistence of an invariant curve)
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a
Diophantine real number and let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be real-analytic, $1$-periodic and
not constant, with $\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx = 0$. Then there is $c_0 > 0$ such that for every real $c$
with $|c| < c_0$ there is a $C^\infty$, strictly increasing function $q : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$
such that $t \mapsto q(t) - t$ is $1$-periodic and, for every real $t$,

$$q(t + \alpha) - 2q(t) + q(t - \alpha) = c\, f(q(t)).$$

## Sources

- A. N. Kolmogorov (1954); V. I. Arnold (1963); J. Moser, *On invariant curves of area-preserving mappings of an annulus*, Nachr. Akad. Wiss. Göttingen (1962). Knill, *Some fundamental theorems in mathematics*, §83. Problem `kam_invariant_curve` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: `V` is constant on the ω-limit set
articles.statement:
If the forward orbit of `x` lies in a compact set
`K` and the continuous function `V` is nonincreasing along it, then there is a constant `c`
(the limit of `V(ϕ t x)`) such that `V(ϕ t y) = c` for every `y ∈ ω⁺(x)` and every `t ≥ 0`.

articles.title: LaSalle's invariance principle
articles.statement:
**LaSalle's invariance principle** (LaSalle 1960; Khalil 2002, Theorem 4.4). Let the forward
orbit of `x` under the semiflow `ϕ` lie in a compact set `K`, let `V` be continuous and
nonincreasing along that orbit, and let `E` contain every `y ∈ K` whose orbit keeps `V`
constant. Then the ω-limit set `ω⁺(x)` is nonempty and contained in the largest
forward-invariant subset `M = {y | ∀ t, ϕ t y ∈ E}` of `E`, and the orbit of `x` eventually
enters every open set containing `M`.

articles.title: Omega-limit set lies in every closed set containing the orbit
articles.statement:
The ω-limit set of a point under a semiflow is contained in every closed set that contains
the forward orbit.

articles.title: Euclidean model space for the shadowing lemma
articles.statement:
For a natural number $d$, $E_d$ is the
Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$, the real $d$-tuples with the Euclidean norm.

articles.title: Shadowing property
articles.statement:
Let $T : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^d$ be a map, write $T^n$ for its
$n$-fold iterate, and let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$. The set $K$ has the shadowing property for
$T$ if there is an open set $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ containing $K$ such that for every
$\delta > 0$ there is $\varepsilon > 0$ with the following property: for every $\varepsilon$-pseudo
orbit $(x_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of $T$ with $x_n \in U$ for all $n$, there is a point
$y \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $\|x_n - T^n(y)\| < \delta$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

articles.title: Anosov–Bowen shadowing lemma
articles.statement:
Let $T : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^d$ be a homeomorphism and
let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a compact set that is a hyperbolic invariant set for $T$. Then $K$
has the shadowing property for $T$.

## Sources

- D.V. Anosov, 'Geodesic flows on closed Riemannian manifolds with negative curvature', Trudy Mat. Inst. Steklov. 90 (1967); R. Bowen, 'ω-limit sets for Axiom A diffeomorphisms', J. Differential Equations 18 (1975) 333–339. Listed as §67 in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `anosov_bowen_shadowing` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Hyperbolic structure
articles.statement:
Let $T : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^d$ be a homeomorphism and let
$K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$. Write $DF_x$ for the derivative of a map $F$ at $x$, $T^n$ for the
$n$-fold iterate of $T$ and $T^{-n}$ for the $n$-fold iterate of $T^{-1}$. A hyperbolic structure
for $T$ on $K$ consists of the following: $T$ and $T^{-1}$ are $C^1$; $T(K) = K$; to every
$x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ are assigned linear subspaces $E^s(x)$ and $E^u(x)$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$ such that
for every $x \in K$ we have $\mathbb{R}^d = E^s(x) \oplus E^u(x)$, $DT_x(E^s(x)) = E^s(T(x))$ and
$DT_x(E^u(x)) = E^u(T(x))$; and there are real numbers $\lambda$ with $0 < \lambda < 1$ and
$C > 0$ such that for every $x \in K$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$,
$\|D(T^n)_x v\| \le C \lambda^n \|v\|$ for all $v \in E^s(x)$ and
$\|D(T^{-n})_x v\| \le C \lambda^n \|v\|$ for all $v \in E^u(x)$.

articles.title: Hyperbolic invariant set
articles.statement:
Let $T : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^d$ be a homeomorphism. A set
$K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is a hyperbolic invariant set for $T$ if there exists a hyperbolic
structure for $T$ on $K$.

articles.title: Pseudo-orbit
articles.statement:
Let $d$ be a natural number, let $\mathbb{R}^d$ carry the Euclidean norm,
let $T : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^d$ be a map and let $\varepsilon$ be a real number. A
sequence $(x_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is an $\varepsilon$-pseudo orbit of $T$
if $\|x_{n+1} - T(x_n)\| < \varepsilon$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

articles.title: Complex eigenvalues of a real linear map
articles.statement:
For a continuous linear map $L$ from
$\mathbb{R}^n$ to itself, the complex eigenvalues of $L$ form the multiset of complex roots of the
characteristic polynomial of $L$, each counted with its multiplicity as a root.

articles.title: Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ for local stable and unstable sets
articles.statement:
For a natural number
$n$, this is the space $\mathbb{R}^n$ of real $n$-tuples with the Euclidean inner product and
norm.

articles.title: Hyperbolic linear map
articles.statement:
A continuous linear map $L$ from $\mathbb{R}^n$ to itself is
hyperbolic when none of its complex eigenvalues lies on the unit circle, that is, every complex
root $\mu$ of the characteristic polynomial of $L$ satisfies $|\mu| \ne 1$.

articles.title: Local stable and unstable sets at a hyperbolic fixed point
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to
\mathbb{R}^n$ be continuously differentiable on a neighbourhood of a point $x_0$ with
$f(x_0) = x_0$, and suppose that the derivative $Df(x_0)$ is invertible and hyperbolic. Then
there is an open set $U$ containing $x_0$ such that the local stable set
$W^s = \{x : f^k(x) \in U \text{ for all } k \ge 0 \text{ and } f^k(x) \to x_0 \text{ as }
k \to \infty\}$ and the local unstable set $W^u$, consisting of the points $x$ for which there
is a sequence $(y_k)_{k \ge 0}$ in $U$ with $y_0 = x$, $f(y_{k+1}) = y_k$ for all $k$ and
$y_k \to x_0$, satisfy $W^s \cap W^u = \{x_0\}$.

This is only the set-level part of the Hadamard–Perron theorem: it does not assert that $W^s$
and $W^u$ are $C^1$ submanifolds tangent to the stable and unstable subspaces of $Df(x_0)$.

## Sources

- J. Hadamard, 'Sur l'itération et les solutions asymptotiques des équations différentielles', Bull. Soc. Math. France 29 (1901); O. Perron, 'Über Stabilität und asymptotisches Verhalten der Integrale von Differentialgleichungssystemen', Math. Z. 29 (1929) 129–160. Listed as §104 in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `stable_unstable_manifolds` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Realizable span of a nondegenerate binary recurrence
articles.statement:
Let $B$ and $C$ be integers with
$C \neq 0$, and suppose the recurrence is nondegenerate: whenever $\alpha \neq \beta$ are
complex roots of $x^2 - Bx + C$, we have $(\alpha/\beta)^n \neq 1$ for every integer $n \geq 1$.
Put $\Delta = B^2 - 4C$. Let $R$ be the set of complex sequences $(u_n)_{n \geq 0}$ coming from
integer sequences $u$ that satisfy $u_{n+2} = B u_{n+1} - C u_n$ for all $n \geq 0$ and for
which there are a set $X$ and a map $T \colon X \to X$ such that, for every $n \geq 0$, the set
of points $x \in X$ with $T^{n+1}(x) = x$ is finite and has exactly $|u_n|$ elements. Then the
complex linear span of $R$ has dimension $0$ if $\Delta < 0$, dimension $1$ if $\Delta = 0$ or
$\Delta > 0$ is not the square of an integer, and dimension $2$ if $\Delta > 0$ is the square
of an integer.

## Sources

- G. Everest, A. J. van der Poorten, Y. Puri, and T. Ward, "Integer Sequences and Periodic Points," Journal of Integer Sequences 5 (2002), Article 02.2.3, Theorem, lines 243–254, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL5/Ward/ward2.tex

articles.title: Aperiodic part of the full 2-shift
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be the left shift on the full 2-shift
$X$, given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$. The aperiodic part of $X$ is the set of all $x \in X$
that are not periodic for $\sigma$, that is, with $\sigma^n x \ne x$ for every $n \ge 1$.

## Sources

- [AMR-043-0001].

articles.title: Aperiodic part of the 3-colouring shift
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be the left shift on the full
3-shift, given by $(\sigma y)_i = y_{i+1}$. The aperiodic part of the proper 3-colouring shift
$Y$ is the set of all $y \in Y$ that are not periodic for $\sigma$, that is, with
$\sigma^n y \ne y$ for every $n \ge 1$.

## Sources

- [AMR-043-0001].

articles.title: The aperiodic parts of the full 2-shift and the 3-colouring shift are not conjugate
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be the full 2-shift, $Y$ the proper 3-colouring shift, and $\sigma$ the left shift on
each. There is no homeomorphism $e$ from the aperiodic part of $X$ onto the aperiodic part of
$Y$, each with the subspace topology, such that $e(\sigma a) = \sigma(e(a))$ for every $a$ in the
aperiodic part of $X$; that is, Hochman's aperiodic conjugacy question has a negative answer.

Salo proves that every conjugacy between infinite transitive shifts of finite type minus
periodic points extends to a conjugacy of the shifts of finite type; since the full 2-shift
has fixed points and the proper 3-colouring shift has none, the aperiodic parts are not
conjugate.

## Sources

articles.title: Hochman's aperiodic conjugacy question
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be the full 2-shift and $Y$ the proper
3-colouring shift, write $X \setminus \mathrm{Per}(X)$ and $Y \setminus \mathrm{Per}(Y)$ for
their aperiodic parts with the subspace topologies, and let $\sigma$ be the left shift
$(\sigma z)_i = z_{i+1}$ on each. The statement is that there is a homeomorphism
$e \colon X \setminus \mathrm{Per}(X) \to Y \setminus \mathrm{Per}(Y)$ with
$e(\sigma a) = \sigma(e(a))$ for every $a \in X \setminus \mathrm{Per}(X)$, that is, the two
aperiodic parts are topologically conjugate.

## Sources

- [AMR-043-0001] Hochman problem 1.

articles.title: Shift on the aperiodic part of the full 2-shift
articles.statement:
The left shift $\sigma$, given by
$(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$, maps the aperiodic part of the full 2-shift $X$ into itself; this is
the self-map of the aperiodic part of $X$ obtained by restricting $\sigma$ to it.

## Sources

- [AMR-043-0001].

articles.title: Shift on the aperiodic part of the 3-colouring shift
articles.statement:
The left shift $\sigma$, given by
$(\sigma y)_i = y_{i+1}$, maps the aperiodic part of the proper 3-colouring shift $Y$ into
itself; this is the self-map of the aperiodic part of $Y$ obtained by restricting $\sigma$
to it.

## Sources

- [AMR-043-0001].

articles.title: The full 2-shift
articles.statement:
$X$ is the space of all two-sided sequences
$x = (x_i)_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$ with every $x_i \in \{0, 1\}$, carrying the product topology.

## Sources

- [AMR-043-0001].

articles.title: The proper 3-colouring shift
articles.statement:
$Y$ is the set of sequences $y = (y_i)_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$
in the full 3-shift (so every $y_i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$) such that $y_i \ne y_{i+1}$ for every
$i \in \mathbb{Z}$.

It is a mixing shift of finite type.

articles.title: The full 3-shift
articles.statement:
The space of all two-sided sequences $y = (y_i)_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$
with every $y_i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, carrying the product topology. It is the ambient space of the
proper 3-colouring shift.

articles.title: Curtis–Hedlund–Lyndon theorem with an arbitrary discrete output alphabet
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
finite set and $B$ any set, both with the discrete topology, and give $A^{\mathbb{Z}}$ and
$B^{\mathbb{Z}}$ the product topology. For $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ let $\sigma^k$ be the shift on
either space given by $(\sigma^k x)_n = x_{n+k}$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$. A map
$F : A^{\mathbb{Z}} \to B^{\mathbb{Z}}$ is a sliding block code, that is, there are a radius
$r \in \mathbb{N}$ and a local rule $\varphi : A^{2r+1} \to B$ with
$F(x)_n = \varphi(x_{n-r}, \dots, x_{n+r})$ for all $x \in A^{\mathbb{Z}}$ and $n \in \mathbb{Z}$,
if and only if $F$ is continuous and commutes with every shift: $F(\sigma^k x) = \sigma^k F(x)$
for all $x \in A^{\mathbb{Z}}$ and $k \in \mathbb{Z}$.

articles.title: Curtis–Hedlund–Lyndon theorem
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets with the discrete
topology, and give $A^{\mathbb{Z}}$ and $B^{\mathbb{Z}}$ the product topology. For
$k \in \mathbb{Z}$ let $\sigma^k$ be the shift on either space given by
$(\sigma^k x)_n = x_{n+k}$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$. A map
$F : A^{\mathbb{Z}} \to B^{\mathbb{Z}}$ is a sliding block code, that is, there are a radius
$r \in \mathbb{N}$ and a local rule $\varphi : A^{2r+1} \to B$ with
$F(x)_n = \varphi(x_{n-r}, \dots, x_{n+r})$ for all $x \in A^{\mathbb{Z}}$ and $n \in \mathbb{Z}$,
if and only if $F$ is continuous and commutes with every shift: $F(\sigma^k x) = \sigma^k F(x)$
for all $x \in A^{\mathbb{Z}}$ and $k \in \mathbb{Z}$.

## Sources

- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curtis%E2%80%93Hedlund%E2%80%93Lyndon_theorem (statement id `curtis-hedlund-s1`).

articles.title: Eventually periodic sequences
articles.statement:
A sequence $u : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ with values in a
type $\alpha$ is eventually periodic if there are natural numbers $p > 0$ (a period) and $n_0$
(a preperiod) such that $u(n + p) = u(n)$ for every natural number $n \ge n_0$.

articles.title: Ultimately periodic sequences
Orbits in a finite set are eventually periodic
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite set, $F : S \to S$ a
map and $r : \mathbb{N} \to S$ a sequence with $r(n + 1) = F(r(n))$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
Then $r$ is eventually periodic.

articles.title: Periodic sequences are eventually periodic
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a type, let
$u : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ be a sequence and let $p > 0$ be a natural number with
$u(n + p) = u(n)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $u$ is eventually periodic.

articles.title: Explicit period and preperiod give eventual periodicity
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a type and
$u : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ a sequence. If there are natural numbers $p > 0$ and $n_0$ such that
$u(n + p) = u(n)$ for every natural number $n \ge n_0$, then $u$ is eventually periodic.

articles.title: Period and preperiod of an eventually periodic sequence
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a type. If a
sequence $u : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ is eventually periodic, then there are natural numbers
$p > 0$ and $n_0$ such that $u(n + p) = u(n)$ for every natural number $n \ge n_0$.

articles.title: Automorphism group of the full shift
articles.statement:
The automorphism group of the full shift on $N$
symbols is the subgroup of the group of homeomorphisms of $\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ onto
itself consisting of the homeomorphisms $\varphi$ that commute with the unit shift $\sigma$,
given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$, that is, $\varphi \circ \sigma = \sigma \circ \varphi$.

articles.title: Full shift space
articles.statement:
For $N \in \mathbb{N}$, the configuration space of the two-sided full
shift on $N$ symbols is the set $\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ of all bi-infinite sequences
$x = (x_i)_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$ of symbols. It carries the product of the discrete topologies.

articles.title: One-dimensional cellular automaton
articles.statement:
A map $f$ from the full shift
$\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ on $N$ symbols to itself is a one-dimensional cellular
automaton if $f$ is continuous and commutes with the unit shift $\sigma$, given by
$(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$, that is, $f \circ \sigma = \sigma \circ f$.

This is the Curtis–Hedlund–Lyndon characterization of cellular automata.

articles.title: Joint periodic count
articles.statement:
For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and a map $f$ from the full shift
$\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ on $N$ symbols to itself, $P(f, k)$ is the number of
configurations $x$ with $\sigma^k(x) = x$, where $\sigma$ is the unit shift given by
$(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$, that are also periodic for $f$, that is, $f^n(x) = x$ for some
$n \ge 1$. Here $k$ need not be the least period of $x$ under $\sigma$.

The count is the cardinality of a set, taken to be $0$ when the set is infinite, which can
happen only for $k = 0$.

articles.title: Joint periodic growth rate
articles.statement:
For a map $f$ from the full shift $S_N$ on $N$ symbols to
itself, the joint periodic growth rate is the real number

$$\nu(f, S_N) = \limsup_{k \to \infty} P(f, k)^{1/k},$$

where $k$ ranges over the positive integers and $P(f, k)$ is the joint periodic count: the
number of configurations fixed by the $k$-th power of the unit shift that are also periodic
for $f$.

articles.title: Jointly periodic points
articles.statement:
For a map $f$ from the full shift
$\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ on $N$ symbols to itself, the jointly periodic points of $f$
are the configurations $x$ that are periodic for $f$ and periodic for the unit shift $\sigma$,
given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$: there are $m \ge 1$ and $n \ge 1$ with $f^m(x) = x$ and
$\sigma^n(x) = x$.

No common period for $f$ and $\sigma$ is required.

articles.title: The unit shift as a homeomorphism
articles.statement:
The unit shift $\sigma$ of the full shift on $N$
symbols, given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$, is a homeomorphism of
$\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ onto itself, with inverse given by
$(\sigma^{-1} x)_i = x_{i-1}$.

articles.title: Unit shift
articles.statement:
The unit shift on the full shift on $N$ symbols is the map $\sigma$ from
$\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ to itself given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$ for all
$i \in \mathbb{Z}$, the left translation by one step.

articles.title: Forward orbit
articles.statement:
For a self-map $f$ of a set $X$ and a point $x \in X$, the forward orbit
of $x$ under $f$ is the set $\{f^n(x) : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ of all iterates of $x$, including
$f^0(x) = x$.

articles.title: Grand orbit relation
articles.statement:
For a self-map $f$ of a set $X$, points $x, y \in X$ are related,
that is, lie in the same grand orbit of $f$, when $f^m(x) = f^n(y)$ for some natural numbers
$m$ and $n$.

articles.title: Grand orbit equivalence relation
articles.statement:
For a self-map $f$ of a set $X$, the relation on $X$ in
which $x \sim y$ when $f^m(x) = f^n(y)$ for some natural numbers $m$ and $n$ is an equivalence
relation; its equivalence classes are the grand orbits of $f$.

articles.title: Grand orbit
articles.statement:
For a self-map $f$ of a set $X$ and a point $x \in X$, the grand orbit of $x$
is the set of all $y \in X$ such that $f^m(x) = f^n(y)$ for some natural numbers $m$ and $n$,
that is, the equivalence class of $x$ under the grand orbit relation.

articles.title: Preperiodic point of a given type
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a self-map of a set $X$ and let $m$ and $n$
be natural numbers. A point $x \in X$ is preperiodic of type $(m, n)$ when $n > 0$ and
$f^{m+n}(x) = f^m(x)$, that is, $f^m(x)$ is periodic with period $n$. Neither $m$ nor $n$ is
required to be minimal.

articles.title: Preperiodic point
articles.statement:
A point $x$ is preperiodic for a self-map $f$ when its forward orbit
$\{f^n(x) : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ under $f$ is a finite set.

articles.title: Strictly preperiodic point
articles.statement:
A point $x$ is strictly preperiodic for a self-map $f$ when it
is preperiodic for $f$ but not periodic, that is, there is no $n > 0$ with $f^n(x) = x$.

articles.title: Furstenberg–Weiss multiple recurrence for a single homeomorphism
articles.statement:
Every homeomorphism
$T$ of a nonempty compact metric space $X$ has a multiply recurrent point: there is a point
$x \in X$ such that for every integer $d \ge 1$ there is a strictly increasing sequence of
natural numbers $(n_k)$ with $T^{j n_k}(x) \to x$ as $k \to \infty$ for every integer $j$ with
$1 \le j \le d$, where $T^{m}$ denotes the $m$-th iterate of $T$.

## Sources

- H. Furstenberg and B. Weiss, *Topological dynamics and combinatorial number theory*, Journal d'Analyse Mathématique 34 (1978), 61-85. Listed as §56 (main theorem) in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `furstenberg_topological` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Multiply recurrent point
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space and $T \colon X \to X$ a map.
A point $x \in X$ is multiply recurrent for $T$ if for every integer $d \ge 1$ there is a
strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers $(n_k)$ such that $T^{j n_k}(x) \to x$ as
$k \to \infty$ for every integer $j$ with $1 \le j \le d$, where $T^{m}$ denotes the $m$-th
iterate of $T$.
